tenures.bio:
Joanna: 

Joanna managed Adien and then tag team partner Bahamut 
From the GWF to the now dead WWA. There they became 
World Tag team Champions till Bahamut decided it was time 
to retire. Adien, at a loss in singles went out in search 
foe his new, and current partner Reod Dai. Together she 
took them to the top again as the WWA World Tag Champions. 
She now is in search for a new fed that her team can dominate. 
What better fed than Anarchy. 

Joanna is about 5'6', wears biking shorts 
and tee shirt, and always has a Studded 
Leather Glove on her right hand. 

Adien Pryde 
Height: 5'10' 
Weight: 245lbs 
Entrance Music: 'Seek 200' by Information Society 
Wears: (Entrance) Black leather jacket with a green falcon carrying a sword on the back.
	(Ring) Black tights with ANARCHY in red down the left side.

Singles Finisher: Falcon Bomb (Lifts his opponent up in the razors edge then flips them over the shoulder and catches their head and drives them down into a DDT.) 
Tag Team Finisher: Total Anarchy (Total Elimination, Pryde foot sweeps from the rear, Dai Spin Wheel kick from the front) 

Adien started his career in the GWF. Fresh out of 
collage, he found out the stark reality that not all 
wrestlers were honorable. After numerous back stabs, 
something in Adien snapped. Now a heel, Adien joined with 
Bahamut, a 7' giant and they were soon dominating the 
Tag Team scene and captured the Titles. Later, they joined 
the WWA after being lost in the GWF split. There they went to 
the top as Dragons Lair and won the WWA World Tag Team Titles. 
Several months after losing the titles, Bahamut retired. Joanna 
decided to get Adien a new partner. Enter Reod Dai, Pit fighter 
and amateur wrestler. Together they formed Anarchy, a team who 
didn't care who they wrestled, as long as they got what they wanted, 
any and all titles. Now he is her to rule the WWA again. 

Reod Dai 
Height: 6'2' 
Weight: 260lbs 
Entrance Music: 'Seek 200' by Information Society
Wears: (Entrance) Long tattered leather trench, large wide brimmed hat, carrying a bo staff 
            (Ring) Black tights with ANARCHY in red down the left side, and a red dragon on the right 

Singles Finisher: Dragon Strike(Blackmen's Lethal Kick to the face) 
Tag Team Finisher: Total Anarchy (Total Elimination, Pryde foot sweeps from the rear, Dai Spin Wheel kick from the front) 

Reod started in the small community of Morristown, MN. A population of 800 people 
was not his idea of a party place. He moved to Minneapolis at the age of 16 
where he started to hang with a rough crowd. Here he learned the anything goes style 
of Pit Fighting. At age 17, Joanna entered his life. She liked what she saw and started 
to manage his career. For 2 years they traveled the country, winning match after match. 
Then it all ended on fateful night. Reod was slammed on his knee on the cement floor. His 
Knee was shattered, and so was his career. The next year, he was to spend in rehab, he 
told Joanna to continue her career. All through the year, Reod could thing of nothing but 
making a comeback. Joanna would keep him up to date on her life, including the new 
Tag Team she had in Pro Wrestling. Then one day, She came to him with an offer. One 
member of her team had retired. Joanna wanted Reod to fill his spot. He agreed on one 
condition. No other allies. From that moment on Anarchy was Born.

tenures.note: THE LINE: a uewf tenure is warranted where a held document BILLS THE ENTITY AS THAT FEDERATION'S OWN, or STAGES IT FOR ONE OF THAT FEDERATION'S OWN CHAMPIONSHIPS. Entry to a tournament held at an interfederation event is not by itself enough — the Summit's tournaments were open to all comers and a bracket slot says only that somebody entered. WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW: the team stands in the UeWF's own published tag-team rankings under its own name, in the ranking tables the WeWF newsdesk reprints from that federation on 30 January, 15 February and 25 February 1992; and its own manager, with the team flanking him on camera, says they were there — "We know all about you, from being in the UeWF, may it rest in peace, together." A place in a federation's own weekly rankings is that federation billing the entity as its own. Three of the WeWF newsdesk editions of 30 January, 15 February and 25 February 1992 reprint the UeWF's own published weekly rankings in full, singles, tag and ladies, and this entity stands in them under its own name. The tenure is not overstated; it is now independently attested from the other wing's shelf.

tenures.bio:
Team: Boogiepop Dynasty







Name:



-Rampage (Ryo Tazawa)



-Cellacia (Reimi Otonachi)



-Kyoshiro (Kyoshiro Kimura)



Birth Dates:



-August 4, 1977 (25)



-May 18, 1981 (21)



-March 23, 1979 (23)



Hometowns:



-Nara, Honshu, Japan



-Kumamoto, Kyuushuu, Japan



-Kochi, Shikoku, Japan



Heights:



-6’2



-5’8



-5’11



Weights:



-284 lbs



-173 lbs



-249 lbs



Nicknames:



-Rampage: ‘Page, Rock Star



-Cellacia: Cell, Boogiepop, J-Pop Princess



-Kyoshiro: Kyo, #1 Slugga



Status: Face

Entrance Music: “Kagami Kamen” (Mirror Mask) by Boogiepop Dynasty (BD’s first single)



Wrestling Styles: 



-Rampage: Technical/Shoot Style wrestling, focusing on suplex and submission chains, working on specific body parts to set up for the kill.



-Cell: High Flying/Gymnastics, lucha libre-like movement through the ring, flipping and spinning acrobatic maneuvers that will land the opponent on the mat. 



-Kyo: Brawling/Martial Arts, a fighter to the end, working on punches and kicks to down his opponent as they do in the streets, hence the name, #1 Slugga



Set Up Move: 



Complete B-Dynasty setup: Fusion Beats: Cell performs a spinning legscissors arm drag (Sickle Cell), followed by Kyo nailing a double axe handle uppercut the opponent into the corner (#1 Slugga). Rampage comes in w/ a splash, but grabs the opponent and throws him over with an overhead belly to belly suplex (1/3 of Retroplex).



Cell/Kyo setup: Hip/Pop: Cell pushes opponent into the ropes and leaps up, grabbing them in a jumping hip toss. The throw sends the opponent over sitting up on the mat, but just as impact is made Kyo comes in with a sliding Karate kick to the face, knocking them down on their face.



Cell/Rampage setup: Heavy Metal Queen: Rampage lifts the opponent up for a Brainbuster, and Cell runs in, leaps up and wraps her legs around the opponent’s upper torso. The weight sends all three down, Rampage in a Brainbuster DDT and Cell in a sitting bearhug piledriver.



Rampage/Kyo setup: The Beatdown: Rampage locks in a full nelson from behind, allowing Kyo to come in with a right cross to the jaw, left hook shot to the midsection, and a final right uppercut to the chin as Rampage goes over w/ the Dragon Suplex.



Cell: Sickle Cell: A spinning legscissors arm drag; Cell runs on the opponent and goes for a spinning legscissors, but spins completely around and morphs the move into a spinning arm drag, sending the opponent into the mat and dizzying them as they rise back up.



Kyo: #1 Slugga: An uppercutting double axe handle smash that knocks the opponent back, mostly aimed so that the opponent falls back into the corner or ropes. 



Rampage: Retroplex: Rampage locks his arms around the opponent and throws them over w/ an overhead belly to belly suplex, but rolls over, squats over the opponent w/ his arms still locked, and pulls the opponent up with another overhead belly to belly. Pulling the opponent back up once more, Rampage turns 180 degrees and nails a releasing belly to belly suplex. 



Finishers:



Complete B-Dynasty finisher: Boogiepop Revolution: Kyo runs in with Da Noise, knocking the opponent back into the waiting arms of Rampage for the Acoustic. Cell comes off with the finishing, jumping up and pinning both of the opponent’s legs to the ground with her own legs and bridges as Rampage bridges the Acoustic.



Rampage: Acoustic: Rampage grabs the opponent in a tiger suplex from behind, locking his hands around the arms in a vertical over horizontal position. Then he locks his hips and snaps the opponent over, slamming them straight onto the back of their head/back. (snap tiger suplex)



Kyo: Da Noise: Kyo runs in with a spinning elbow smash (roaring elbow) into the temple of the opponent, knocking them back onto the mat out cold. 



Cell: Idol Hands: Cell locks hands with the opponent and leaps up for a hurricanrana. Cell then rolls over so that she is back to back with her opponent, hands still locked. Then she pulls herself back and locks her legs around the person’s neck, flipping them over for a reverse rana into an sitout mat slam/x-factor.



Cell/Kyo finisher: Gentle Verse: Cell performs the Idol Hands, but just as she goes to complete the final portion, Kyo runs in and delivers Da Noise, adding extra impact to the reverse rana/x-factor from Cell.



Cell/Rampage finisher: Uncut Version: Rampage goes for the Acoustic, and just as he snaps the opponent over Cell flips over with a somersault axe kick into the throat of the opponent, a double impact on the neck from both sides. 



Rampage/Kyo finisher: Amp Frequency: Rampage prepares for the Acoustic, and Kyo adds in extra power to the move with  #1 Slugga right under the chin before Rampage completes his move.



Kyo Move set-



Kimura Slide: Kyo slides in through the legs of the opponent, grabbing the ankles and pulling them down face first into the mat. 



7th Inning: Moving in with a back elbow thrust into the midsection, Kyo grabs the back of the head and holds it as he comes up with a knee into the face of the opponent. Then he closes it with a side shuffle kick into the face, knocking them back into the mat. 



Street Pitcher: Kyo throws the opponent into the ropes, and when they come back he nails them under the chin with a thrust kick. The opponent falls back into the ropes, and Kyo catches them on the rebound, grabbing them by the neck and throws them down with a judo hip toss on the mat.



Bases Loaded: A spear into a mounted punch set, Kyo tackling the opponent before kneeling over them and pummeling them with both fists. 



Fastball: Known in the streets for his quick hands, Kyo comes around with a quick roundhouse hook across the face of the victim. Usually used around the end of a punching comeback, or as a sudden counter against strikes. 



Cell Move set-



White Cell: Jump Swinging Hurricanrana; Cell runs at the opponent, and jumps up, swinging around the person like a jump swinging DDT, but when she comes around to the front of the opponent, she leaps up and nails them with a swift hurricanrana. 



Red Cell: Cell leaps up, grabbing the person’s head and leaning back into a DDT, but Cell adds more impact as she monkey flips the opponent over, putting more force into the DDT



J-Pop: A counter as well as an attack; Cell grabs the opponent and whips them away, but holds onto them. She yanks them back and presses her back against the person’s chest, snatching the opponent over in a modified judo hip toss/rotating fireman’s carry. A counter if whipped and she reverses.



Idol Image: Cell leaps up for a hurricanrana, but spins around so that she faces the same way as the victim. Then she hangs down, her ankles around the opponent’s head as she reaches under and grabs the opponent’s legs, pulling the opponent’s head down into the mat as they drop down to their knees. A pin attempt can be made if she rolls over as she has the legs hooked.



Cellibate: A 360 rotating high angle bulldog. Cell grabs the opponent for a bulldog and runs up the turnbuckle or ropes, springing off in a back flip and drives the opponent back down in a high angle bulldog, Cell landing straight on her back w/ her legs up in the air. Can be used as a counter to a back drop or variation of a back drop.



Rampage Move set-



Emo Flux: Rampage tackles the opponent in the back, knocking them forward into either the mat, the ropes, or the corner. Then he wraps his arms around their waist and nails a snapping overhead German Suplex, Rampage arches over and presses them facedown into the mat to add impact. Optional methods include rolling over and continuing the snapping overhead German suplex chain, bridging for a pin, or rolling over and nailing a releasing suplex.



Heavy Metal: The opponent is snatched up onto Rampage’s shoulders in a fireman’s carry. Then Rampage completely drops backwards, crashing down in a bridging Samoan Drop. Optional methods bridging for a pin, rolling over and nailing another Samoan Drop suplex in chain, or rolling over and nailing a front flipping Samoan Drop suplex. 



Guitar Vader: With the opponent face down on the mat, Rampage locks the arm in a leg scissors armbar, while grabbing the other arm and locking in a half chickenwing. Then he takes his free right arm and leans over, pulling back on the neck of the opponent. (Crossface Chickenwing Armbar Submission.)



Screech and Thrash: Rampage locks in a sharpshooter, and leans back, lodging his knee into the back of the victim and wrenching on the back in a elevated Boston Crab variation. 



Alternative Hype: Locking in a reverse full nelson hold, Rampage throws the opponent over in a reverse Dragon Suplex. Can be chained into multiple suplexes and can be bridged. 













History—



Cellacia Otonachi, Rampage, and Kyoshiro…



The sweet and down to earth brown and white haired girl next door…



The big-hearted and skilled blonde muscle-bound jock…



The rough, cocky, and raspy boy from the streets w/ half a foot tall hairdo…



You probably know these three as friends of the infamous Inphino Blitz, martial artist known throughout the world. But now the group known formerly as the Blitz Promotional Team is taking their chance to make themselves known in two very different ways. 



These three, veterans of puro from the Tokyo Wrestling League, have taken the opportunity to show their wares in the newly reopening PURE, using their past accolades along with their ties to Inphino Blitz and PURE player Mina de Margo to ensure themselves a position within the company…more importantly, to help establish the unique Trinity Division and make it a success.



Their second chance at stardom is in the form of their music. Each of these three members brings a personal touch of musical genius to the group…Cell the J-Pop Princess, Rampage the Rock Star, and Kyo the Verse Villain and the “#1 Slugga” as he is known on the streets. Rap, Pop, and Rock…merged into one entity that they have dubbed:



“Boogiepop Dynasty”



After auditioning for Naoki Records out of Kamakura, the CEOs of the company, the sibling duo of Debutante and Dilettante Masaki, signed these three right away. It wasn’t soon that the same song they auditioned with was released as the group’s first single; Kagami Kamen, or Mirror Mask. The song’s topped charts through the country, and has made good reviews on the foreign markets. Naoki Records has high hopes that their wrestling career will also bring more publicity to the group, as well as increase CD and merchandising sales.



Of course to Cell, Rampage, and Kyo, it’s all about the fans…it’s all about the fight…it’s all about the music. 



You are now under the will of the Boogiepop Dynasty…

tenures.note: Appended rather than minted fresh: an original character carried by its handler across promotions is one continuous life, one row. The UeWF's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 names Carnage — "Crash and Burn" — as its Intercontinental Tag Team Champions, and Lord Plunder as its Pacific Champion; the WeWF's own broadcast of 13 April 1992, served under that wing, has the same three in the same combination, Crash and Burn as Carnage with Lord Plunder managing them. Name, full membership, window and community all agree. A third document in the held record but not served — the WeWF's own tag tournament broadcast of 24 March 1992 — bills Carnage outright as "the UeWF InterContinental Tag Team Champions," which is a single document naming both sides of the join. It was served on promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-tv-tag-team-tournament-round-2-1992-03-24.html, where the ring announcer's own words read "here are the UeWF InterContinental Tag Team Champions," and Burn adds "me and Burn got two of them". The join is now attested by a served page on this wing's own shelf.

They beat the Blondes for the belts, Cattley pinning Flash Savage with the Mood Swing, and keep them against Antonio & Raphael at Leap Into The Unknown in February, the Blondes at Third Time's The Charm in March and Thrash and Firebird at April Showers; in April 2011 Cattley tells the narrator and Rip Chord that he is leaving for the SWF. The diary's own title records list the reign as "Cattley & Singh January 2011 3". They lose the Tag Team titles to the Canadian Blondes at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, Oscar Golden pinning Cattley; Casey Valentine and Antonio attack them and Erik Strong makes his return, and Cattley then loses a Loser Leaves Town match to Valentine and leaves MAW.

units.name: the Flash Brothers

tenures.source: the fed's own served bio page (cross-referenced from the already-served cwfpro archive)
tenures.note: Own bio's own History section, in full: "They were the main tag team in the XXX with Bryan Williams, Bobby Williams and Star but never really got along with them. The 1st XXX was not own by Pres Burns. Untill he bought it in 2003 after it had shut down. He reopened it as a farm efed for the cwf.pro untill he would close it again in 2006." (The "Star" named alongside Bryan/Bobby Williams here is not confidently identified — Jason Star's own bio dates his own XXX involvement to a 2006 developmental contract, after the farm era began, so this row is not given an XXX-first tenure on that loose thread alone.) Their own Earlier Career line separately dates their DEPARTURE from the XXX to 2001 ("They left the XXX efed after talking with R@ven in 2001"), before the 2003 buy this same passage states — read as the same wrestlers' XXX run ending before the promotion itself changed hands, not a contradiction. SOURCES DISAGREE with bobby-williams's own tenure note on the buy date (2003 vs. 2005) — both are recorded, neither resolved. FURTHER, THIS PASS — A DATE THE ACCESSION DID NOT CARRY: their own Earlier Career line ends their independent-XXX run precisely, and names who ended it. "They started out in 1997 as rookies in a few efeds winning minor titles in the PWE, JJP, GWC, & RFP. They left the XXX efed after talking with R@ven in 2001." R@ven is the buyer's own scout (his own served bio: "He was a scouter for the cwf.pro"), and the same page's next section confirms what the talking was for: "They were set to join the CWF-Pro in 2001, but the cwf.pro clsed after the cross over with the tdw." That gives this wing its only firmly dated in-era EVENT of any kind — a departure in 2001, inside the independent XXX's own attested 2000-2003 window, two years before the earlier of the two disputed buyout years. Note also that the four efeds named as their 1997 starting points (PWE, JJP, GWC, RFP) are NOT the XXX; nothing here moves this wing's own founding date earlier than Bobby Williams' own 2000. Every XXX championship credit carried by any of this wing's three roster entities was counted against the five served XXX title ledgers, all of which are dated uniformly "1/2006 - 11/2007" and belong to the post-buyout farm era. EVERY CREDIT RECONCILES EXACTLY, leaving no residue that could belong to the independent promotion: Bobby Williams' own "XXX Champion (3)" against xxx-title.html's reigns 2, 11 and 14; his "XXX 2nd Champion (5)" against xxx-2nd-title.html's reigns 2, 4, 6, 15 and 17; his "XXX Tag Team Champion" against xxx-world-tag-team-title.html's reign 36 (with Jason Star). Bryan Williams' own "XXX Champion (4)" against reigns 1, 8, 10 and 13 — matching that ledger's own summary table, "Most Times as Champion: Bryan Williams, 4 times" — and his "XXX 2nd Champion (2)" against reigns 5 and 10. The Flash Brothers' own "XXX World Tag Team Champions (15)" against that ledger's own summary table, "Most Times as Champions: Flash Brothers, 15 times," and their "XXX 2nd Tag Team Champions (2)" against both of xxx-2nd-tag-team-title.html's own Flash reigns. The independent XXX's own championship record, if it kept one, therefore leaves no trace anywhere in the surviving record — a checked negative, not an unexamined gap.

units.notes: PTCpedia names this team's finisher per federation — the Blackball (a flapjack from Cobb into a cutter from Korver) at PRIME and the Blutarski Bomb (a diving powerbomb into a neckbreaker) at AWC and Global — and lists the Fratricide as a SIGNATURE move rather than the finisher, describing it as a sidewalk slam from Cobb with a springboard or turnbuckle leg drop from Korver. LOW's own bio card, which this record holds, calls the Fratricide the finisher and describes it the other way round, as a back body drop from Korver with a spinning powerbomb from Cobb. Both readings stand (#sources-disagree). PTCpedia's own three articles for this team and its two members (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-delta-upsilon-iota.html, ptcpedia-colby-korver.html and ptcpedia-hank-cobb.html, all captured 20 Aug 2010) are one filled-in template repeated three times — which is why the census's own cross-index paired them as candidate duplicates; they are a tag team and its two members, not one person, and this record's own merge assertion against PRIME's card already carries the join. As the wiki's own secondary account the three articles agree on LOW, AWC, Global and PRIME as the federations, the LOW Tag Team Championship as the only title, "Master of Puppets" by Metallica as the entrance, Digital Mortality (Global) and Jimmy Bonafide (PRIME) as allies and Jason Natas (PRIME) as the rival, and they add three PRIME pay-per-view appearances — Colossus V (with Jimmy Bonafide against Jason Natas and MegaJob), UltraViolence 2008 (against Team V.I.A.G.R.A. and Risk & Reward) and Culture Shock 2008 (as The Dual Halo). units.caption: The stable Triple D announces on the Monday of Week 3, September 2007, after Blaze of Glory, with Seduction, Danny Jillefski, Human Arsenal, Fumihiro Ota, Big Cat Brandon and Jacob Jett ("One word, survival"), to take over USPW; Art Reed signs with Seduction on the Monday of Week 4, and The Hotshots come to Devine as apprentices who are not yet members. A reader calls it Team Seduction renamed. In October 2007 Triple D calls the group to a meeting from which Seduction, Jacob Jett, Art Reed, Human Arsenal and Fumihiro Ota walk out; its members attack Muffin and Sam Strong and turn on Maxmillion Productions. In October 2007 Triple D announces Akima as the group's newest member after Akima kicks Umaga; on Thursday, Week 1, November Seduction, Human Arsenal and Fumihiro Ota turn against Devine, who calls a meeting on the Family Night of Week 2 ("who is with Divinity?") and is told at Pilgrimage that he is not its leader; at Pilgrimage Danny Jillefski makes The Hotshots its newest members, and Jillefski, who has taken over USPW, opens the Monday of Week 3 with the group around him. From the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3, November 2007 to the Monday of Week 4, December 2007 the group tears itself apart: Devine strikes Seduction for saying she leads it and slams a door on Human Arsenal's forearm, Arsenal, Ota and The Hotshots beat Devine down in the hall, Arsenal quits and is talked back in, Devine pays Maxmillion Productions to unmask the Masked Man and puts Wolf Hawkins in the ring in a bag, and by the Monday of Week 4 Devine gives Seduction a week to choose between him and the grave.

tenures.style: Basho is opposite to Ukyo, a shoot-fighter based tactician. He revolves his offense around a Ground and Pound technique, take the opponent down with technical maneuvers and beat him into submission with stiff strikes. He uses his share of power moves, not to mention a few hard kicks to the chin and face to knock the opponent down. His defense involves reversing grapples, and countering strikes with harder strikes of his own. In Japan he used to be known as "Three Strikes" because no one could stand against his three-strike combo; no one has been left standing.

The Summit of E-Wrestling's own third night walks this team to the ring, "Led towards the ring by their shop steward, Molly Maguire… Representing the AFL-CIO", and the PWA's own 1992 record names "Molly MaGuire, shop-steward for Flint and Steel": one woman, one job, one named team, two federations. Debut card, 16 Dec 1997: the tag team Sweet Stuff (Juicy Fruit and Butt-A-Cup) beat the Horsemen's Tiny and Stupendous Steve for the EFW US Tag Team Championship; the Jolly Gay Giant led the group's entrance and wrestled EFW's Dante to a double countout. Little Rich made his EFW debut on the 21 Dec 1997 card against Horsemen enforcer Ice Century, losing by submission; the same night's limousine vignette with Coach Dike supplies the group's own catchphrase ('When you're GWO, you're GWO... 4 Life!'). The Jolly Gay Giant entered the Season's Beatings PPV's ten-man battle royal, and Sweet Stuff lost the US Tag Team Titles back to the Horsemen the same night (29 Dec 1997, Stupendous Steve's MoonPlex on Butt-A-Cup).

tenures.bio:
Chad Matthews

-------------

“Chad Matthews…”

“Who is Chad Matthews?” I hear you cry… as you look through these documents and begin to wonder. Well, Chad Matthews… for the time being anyway, is a nobody… plain and simple, he is a nobody… but, regardless of that wonderful little tidbit of information, I think that you all deserve to discover how this individual came to be the man that he IS today…



Our story begins on Friday 18th August 1981…



Yes, to those of you who have been able to look at the above details… that day just happens to be the ‘Birthdate’ of our little wannabe here…



Anyway, the story starts on the day that Chad Matthews was brought into this world. His mother and father looked upon him and hoped that he’d be the best of their three sons… despite the advantage that they already had upon him, both Mr and Mrs Matthews were convinced that their son would be following the rest to higher plateaus before anyone would even come to recognize it.



How ironic would that statement be later in his life…



Chad progressed through his earlier years of life like any other kid would… well, any other kid that was able to enjoy the company of two older brothers. To introduce the ‘Brothers Grimm’, Joseph and Max were twins… Max being the older of the two, by all of an hour. Our ‘heroic’ figure of Chad tended to live in peace with his older siblings, although there would be times where altercations were inevitable…



The Great Food Fight of Max’s 11th Birthday…

The Punch-Up of Christmas 1990…



And more famously…

The Karaoke Brawl of Summer 1997…



The later event will be detailed later on, but for now… we’ll go back to the relationship that existed between both Chad and his brothers.



As it was said, the three siblings managed to live in peace for the majority of the time and like any unit, they would always try something together. The reason for this is still unknown, but like three best friends who would never leave the other behind… for some incidents, they would all give the task a shot, just to keep the balance of ‘Power’ equal.



The first major task that all three brothers attempted to do was that of ‘Professional Wrestling’. Despite there being a three year gap between Chad and his brothers, by the time that they wanted to start working the business, Chad had developed into an eager sixteen year old chick magnet and his brothers had walked the steps to hitting their early twenties.



Throughout the beginning of his training, Chad found it impossible to keep up with the things that were being done by everyone else… his body just didn’t seem to be ready to handle the strain and stress of fighting inside the ring… however, he persevered, using the goal of one day bettering his brothers as the only incentive needed to push his body through such vile actions…



Remember how the parents of Chad had said how their son would rise through the ranks like nothing before him? Oh… he rose through the ranks of the academy alright… getting used to the basic spots and offence a lot quicker than his brothers and fellow classmates. After a year of training, everyone had decided that Matthews was ready to be used in their independent promotion, working the curtain jerkers to see what kind of effect the lad would have on the crowd…



It was supposed to be the greatest night of his life…

It was supposed to be the moment that he had always dreamed of… ever since stepping in that ring…

It was supposed to be… the moment that his family would be proudest of him…



Chad worked the match… he was strong, he looked alright… but a part of him was missing that night… that part of him that was family love. Chad knew his family didn’t make the show that night… he could see the gap that was supposed to contain their bodies in the crowd.



Depressed…

Distraught…

Disturbed…



Chad Matthews blew a spot in the bout… he was all set to take a DDT… but something happened, he lost his footing while trying to think of his family and was subsequently drilled headfirst into the canvas…



After that night, Matthews decided to call what he thought was quits from the business… he just didn’t have the heart to keep wrestling if none of his family were going to be around to share this moment with him…



It was six months after this night that he found a new love… a new passion, a new something that would give him the chance to shine without the worry of his parents… this was something that he didn’t need support of family for… it was something that he’d be able to express himself in… and gain recognition from more than just his forgotten family… but all of the country…



Pop music… an ever-expanding empire, never willing to reject a talent that can bring money for their company… and fame for themselves.



Chad had kept one thing secret from everyone when he was growing up… that secret was the fact that he could actually sing. People that sing in the showers… sing when listening to music with headphones… sing in general, Chad did everything of the kind when he was sure that nobody would be around to listen to him.



March 25th 1999…



This too would mark a significant date for Chad… not only would it establish the moment that “PoP Worldwide” was created, but it would also establish the date that Chad Matthews met a fledging artist like himself… the only major difference being that this man was Japanese… and not your average member of the human community…



“Hallo… my name is Kamui Fukamachi… I’ve heard some girls talking about your… ability to sing… and I was wondering if you would be willing to join me…”



Ok… Ok… so things didn’t happen as something as the ‘text extract’ above, but the basic jest of things happened and Kamui effectively asked for Chad to become his partner in business, touring the country… singing to the fans, trying to make something out of what they’d both considered to be wasted lives…



June 15th 1999…

July 22nd 1999…

September 28th 1999…

December 24th 1999…

January 1st 2000…



The above dates, just a few of the times that Chad and Kamui were asked to perform at various functions and what-not. Sure, these boys hadn’t marketed themselves as super material… proclaiming that they were going to be bigger than the World itself… but that didn’t stop them from proclaiming they were the biggest party act going at the moment!



Most orders just assumed that the Canadian/Japanese combination would have been a lot funnier than talent flowing… but that was something that never seemed to come true at any of their shows. Chad Matthews had made something of himself… but even with all the success of being a Party Act… the part of him that longed for the business that was Professional Wrestling called out to him… it cried out for him to go back…



An omen…

A Sign…

A Dealing of Fate?



Nobody knows… not even Chad would be able to answer the question for you himself… but, what he can do, is look up to the Stars on any night and say the words…



“My path is chosen… I did it alone… no longer will I hold myself on people… for it will be my undoing once more…”



Will he come to realize a combination of Musical and Wrestling success in PURE? You’ll just have to stay tuned to find out...

Kamui Fukamachi

------------

“Kamui Fukamachi…”



Unlike his ‘Friend’… Kamui was nothing like the individual that Chad was… no way, no how… like two different books… they had different stories, they had different chapters… hell, the only thing about them that was the same was their gender… and possibly their love for everything that is PoP…



This story begins in a small town in Japan, the actual name of the location is information that Kamui refuses to release… and continues to pass himself off as coming from America. Regardless, he was born to parents that died while he was at a young age. Did this event do as much as to haunt the young child?



Of course it did…

Of course it did…



Kamui moved into an Orphanage at the age of three, taken in by ‘Police Officers’ that found him roaming the empty halls of the home that used to belong to his mother and father. Fukamachi was labelled as the “Kid with Big Dreams” while he was at the Orphanage… they accused him of being too adventurous… too hopeful… too ‘high’ on a future that many people believed would never change… for him, or themselves.



They say that sometimes, you need ONE best friend… ONE person to help you up when you fall…



At the age of ten, Kamui thought that he’d meet that one person… the one individual that would change the pathway of his life… that one soul who would never be able to desert him, not even in his darkest hour…



After seven years in the Orphanage, Kamui had met Mai Fuma, a young girl who had also lost her parents… one way or another. Both aged ten, they became what was the best of friends… doing everything that they could think of together…



She was his Rod of Power…

He was her Tower of Hope…



They meant so much to one another…

They meant everything…



Infact, Kamui became so infatuated with his friend, that he began to serenade her with songs that were sung by the other people around the complex. His graceful voice gave her something to feel… something to hold onto… while not in the physical sense, she took his ability… and enjoyed every second it was in motion…



However…

Like many things before this… like many stories before this one…

When there are two people… happy… excited… caring about each other to points that were previously unimaginable… heartbreak is bound to strike… and for Kamui, it couldn’t have struck at a more horrid moment in his life…



September 1992…

A month that will be forever etched in the memory of Kamui… a month that will always stand the test of time, no matter how long our ‘hero’ decides to live for…



Why the lack of a date?



Simple… he doesn’t remember what day it happened… well, that, or the fact that he doesn’t want to remember the exact day that it happened. We could go into a lot of detail about the events of that time… but it wouldn’t be anything worthwhile… after all, whats done is done… and you can’t regret it…



Aside from the horror behind this date… it was also a turning point for our fourteen year old hero… yes, he decided to take the one thing that bonded him to Mai… and developed from that day forth. For some reason, Kamui was confident that he could connect with people of the other-realm in one way or another… and he himself, tried to believe that his music was the bond that existed between both him and Mai…



A fact of Fukamachi…

A sugar coated dream…

A non-existant hope?



Whatever it is… it’s the one thing that Kamui has left with regards to Mai… his last ever item, his last connection with her.



The time went by following that… Kamui perfected his singing talents… he also learned how to fight, namely to protect himself whenever that sticky situation would arise. Fukamachi wanted to be sure that nothing like Mai would ever be allowed to happen to him again… he wasn’t going to lose another friend…



March 25th 1999…



This too would mark a significant date for Kamui… not only would it establish the moment that he had made it to the country of Canada, but it would also be the first time that he met his future ‘Best Friend’ Chad Matthews.



“Hallo… my name is Kamui Fukamachi… I’ve heard some girls talking about your… ability to sing… and I was wondering if you would be willing to join me…”



Ok… Ok… so things didn’t happen as something as the ‘text extract’ above, but the basic jest of things happened and Kamui effectively asked for Chad to become his partner in business, touring the country… singing to the fans, trying to make something out of what they’d both considered to be wasted lives…



June 15th 1999…

July 22nd 1999…

September 28th 1999…

December 24th 1999…

January 1st 2000…



The above dates, just a few of the times that Chad and Kamui were asked to perform at various functions and what-not. Sure, these boys hadn’t marketed themselves as super material… proclaiming that they were going to be bigger than the World itself… but that didn’t stop them from proclaiming they were the biggest party act going at the moment!



Most orders just assumed that the Canadian/Japanese combination would have been a lot funnier than talent flowing… but that was something that never seemed to come true at any of their shows. Kamui had made something of his life along with Chad, they’d both managed to conquer the world of Independent PoP… but what about the hidden agenda that had been carried with Chad?



Matthews wanted to wrestle…

Kamui decided that he wanted to just put his skills to use…



Would it happen… would it ever?



PURE is the place they are now… the next step of the story is down to them and them alone…

tenures.note: Wins the VWF Tag Team Championship from the Rodeo Boys in a Flashback ambush on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminated from the Dog Day One tag team battle royal before winning the Dog Days Tag Team Elimination match. Wins the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round over Sonicman and Sebastian, then joins Flash in beating down the Rodeo Boys during a special Flashback on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) before competing in the sixteen-man tag scramble. Returns to the VWF at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), interrupting the retiring Sebastian and G-Gangsta's own post-match celebration and attacking them, only for both Legends to fight the pair off with a Legend Killer and a Gangsta Smash. Runs in on Mark McQueen during his own VWF Tag Team Championship challenge with Thunder Valenkov at End Of March (30 March 2005), Stevie Knight and Austin Lee hitting the Property Boom to help champions Team Brittania escape by disqualification. Wins a VWF Tag Team Championship match against Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov, the previous champions, at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), when Valenkov turns on his own partner McQueen; a returning Chris Wheeling reveals himself as the agent behind the turn and presents the team new contracts.

units.caption: "All That" Austin Lee and "Hotstuff" Stevie Knight, the reigning VXW Tag Team Champions, retaining the titles by disqualification against Purgatory and Team Brittania at Vegas Violence V, then losing a non-title four-way tornado tag to Purgatory at Fear Is Coming II. Both men entered the Rage In The Cage main event at Phear Phantastic 2005 as co-champions; Austin Lee pinned his own partner Stevie Knight for the match's own first fall, an outcome the broadcast leaves unresolved as to the tag titles' own status. The promotion's own management publicly rejected a stripping rumor on Setting Sun I, confirming Hot Property retained the titles; the team then survived a Tornado Tag Team title defense against The O'Malley Brothers on Christmas Comes Early that ended in a double-pin with no official decision rendered. Retained the VXW Tag Team Championship in a scored Irish Street Fight over The O'Malley Brothers on New Years Eve Of Destruction, Chris Wheeling's own hired men delivering the deciding points. Ran in against the O'Malley Brothers on Winter War II, then teamed with Thunder Valenkov on Winter War III in a losing effort against the Society of Doom that cost the trio a shot at the tag and 24 Hour titles at Ghost Town Blues.

units.name: Internet Favourites

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the team from /promotions/maw-10-simple-rules/archive/show-spring-fever-2009-04-p99-102.html.

units.caption: Max Mayhem and Hugh Lee, who top an internet poll of the company's most entertaining wrestlers in April 2009 and sign Dawn as their manager; they work the Beach Blast three-way and are booked against C-V-2 on the card for Fall Of The King. They lose a first title challenge to C-V-2 at Fall Of The King in September 2009, lose to the Canadian Blondes a month later and to Antonio & Raphael at March Madness in March 2010, and join Fumihiro Ota in April 2010 to challenge The Firm for the Trios titles. They challenge Valentine & Johnson for the Tag Team titles at Beach Blast in July 2010, in a three-way at Back To School and again at Fall Of The King, lose to Antonio & Raphael at All The Leaves Are Brown, and with Amazing Fire Fly lose a trios match to Glamour And Devastation and Nelson Callum at Where It All Begins Again in October. They lose to the Canadian Blondes on the 11th December 2010 tour show and to Firebird and Evil Spirit at Season's Beatings, beat Zeshin Makioka and Yusuke Takahama, Glamour And Devastation and Evil Spirit and Ultimo Soetsu on the 4th January 2011 tour show, lose to the Canadian Blondes at All Or Nothing and to Glamour And Devastation at April Showers, where Findlay O'Farraday clamps a Choke Sleeper on Max Mayhem. They beat Glamour And Devastation on 18th May, Team XDW II on 11th July, Roderick Remus and Nelson Callum on 11th August, Remus and Raphael on 4th September and Jared Johnson and Raphael on 18th September, and lose to Providence and JD Morgan at Hotter Than Hot and to Callum and Raphael on 11th September. They lose to the Canadian Blondes on the 24th October 2011 tour show, to Lockdown at Eleventh Hour on 12th November, when Aaron Andrews springs the match on them, and again to the Blondes on 5th January 2012. They lose to the Second Sons at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March 2012 and are in the four-team Tag Team number-one-contender match at April Showers on 5th April. In the diary's pages for June 2012 the narrator reports that Max Mayhem's contract has lapsed and that Hugh Lee has been re-signed for three months without a partner, so the Internet Favourites are no more.

tenures.source: MWE's own served text throughout. Membership is spelled out twice: promotions/mwe/rp/a-crash-course-in-wrasslin.html (the fed's own board, s4.zetaboards.com/MWEntertainment, via the Wayback Machine) names "the JEST'ers, James Whitman (David's cousin), best friends Eddie Sanchez and Scott Jones, and Thomas Williams (James' best friend)", and promotions/mwe/rp/the-final-flight-of-a-wasted-mind.html expands the acronym itself -- "the JESTers' (James Eddie Scott Thomas) company; JEST Kiddin' inc." Staged on MWE's own cards at promotions/mwe/archive/crowning-glory-2009-08-30.html (the four walk out to "Welcome to the Jungle", have Ryan Adams and David Ferrera ejected from the announce desk on the General Manager's say-so, and run the broadcast for the David Whitman vs. Alejandro Rodriguez retirement match themselves) and promotions/mwe/archive/crowning-glory-ii-2008-08-10.html (all four picked out by the arena camera in the Hall of Fame audience, two of them in a pre-taped titantron segment). Billed from the ring at promotions/mwe/archive/independence-day-2009-07-05.html as "David's cousin's stable the JEST'ers". Thirteen further served MWE roleplays name the unit.
tenures.note: The dates span the earliest and the latest held MWE document that names the unit -- promotions/mwe/rp/pre-turmoil-turmoil.html and promotions/mwe/rp/elephant-in-the-room.html. They are a held-record span, not a stated formation or break-up; MWE's own record gives neither. The group is WcE's, and MWE's own text says so every time it bills them, but the unit is filed here because MWE's own documents are where it is staged -- WcE holds no document of its own.

This is a four-man stable whose name is an acronym of its own members' first names (James, Eddie, Scott, Thomas), spelled out in MWE's own text; none of the four is a court-jester gimmick and no document anywhere names any of them alongside this unit. In April 2007 Los Guerreros beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick (Eddie's Frog Splash on London), lose to Los Increibles, and at Cyberslam are the first team eliminated in the three-way dance for the tag title number one contendership, by the Dudley Boys with 3Ds and a Spike Powerbomb through tables. In the World Cup of July 2007 Eddie and Chavo Guerrero Jr. lead Team Mexico, and the diary's previews for August name Los Guerreros as the third challengers for the Dudley Boyz's Dudleyville Hardcore Titles. On Revolution in August 2007 Los Guerreros challenge the Dudley Boyz for the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles and lose to a 3D on Chavo, the second generation of Dudleyz playing a large part in the result.

units.name: Los Increibles

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-10-p244-324.html.

units.caption: Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera, who end their best-of-seven series at Anarchy Rulz with a hug and team up as Los Increibles on the first Revolution of October 2006, beating Michael Shane and Frankie Kazarian with a Double Springboard Legdrop, and win again with a Double Toprope Guillotina the week after. As part of Team Mexico they lose the Lucha Libre six-man tag at Living Dangerously; after the Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire they turn on Eddie Guerrero with a Hurricanrana, and in April they beat Los Guerreros on Revolution with the Juvi Driver on Eddie and lose the rematch on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In April 2007 Los Increibles beat Los Guerreros on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Rey Mysterio Jr.'s Tornado DDT on Chavo) to earn a tag title match at Cyberslam, where the Whole F**kin' Show keep the belts in the Ladder Match. In May AJ Styles pins Juventud Guerrera on his debut, and in June Juvi beats AJ in a non-title match after AJ kisses Francine, while Rey Mysterio Jr. loses to AJ's low blow and small package. In June 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr. prepares for the World Cup with Team Mexico while Juventud Guerrera, who is not in the tournament, loses to AJ Styles with the low blow and the foot-on-the-rope finishes; in August Juvi beats Rey in the first match of their revived series with a 450 Splash. At Guilty As Charged in October 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr., saying that Juventud Guerrera 'was dead weight' and the reason they never won the tag titles, joins the four-way Stairway To Hell Match for the World Television Championship, and Guerrera, returning through the crowd with a chair, hits all four men; the next night he beats Mysterio with a 450 Splash. In November 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera, who 'cannot stand one another', are booked together against Ultimo Dragon and Christopher Daniels on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and the alliance breaks down when Mysterio floors his own partner with a punch; Guerrera pins Daniels with a 450 Splash.

tenures.role: tag team — billed as Luis Sangre & Ashley Maximoff
tenures.finisher: 1: Hellfire and Brimstone 2: Baño Sangre (Luis's) 3: Faith (Ash's) — 1: Inverted, power bomb/unprettier combination move. 2: Sangre slingshots himself to the top in one fluid motion and leaps off with a 540 degree splash. 3: She does a moonsault from the top rope and over rotates, so she lands back first on her opponent instead of chest first.
tenures.bio:
Luis- Luis Cesar Sangre was a small time musician, just trying to lead a good life.  One fateful night, a infamous gang rode into town and started some trouble in the bar Luis was working in.  Being the good hearted man he is, Luis rushed in to stop them.  What occurred next still haunts the man to this day.  The gang brutually mangled Luis's right hand with a sledgehammer and torched his home with his mother still inside.  After years of rehibilitation, Luis is out to gain revenge on the men who caused him so much pain and one man in particular, Juan Miguel, who has risen through the ranks during that time to become leader of the gang.  With the help of the unusual nun, Sister Ash, Luis searches the world for his target.  He wrestles along the way to pay expenses and to give him free passage to many foreign countries.



Ash- The young woman, by the name of Ash, awoke one morning in a monestary in Mexico with her memories gone and her past a mystery.  With nowhere else to turn, Ash stayed with the sisters and was taught how to be a woman of god.  As Ash stayed with in the nunery, she started to notice a difference between her and the other nuns.  She was faster and stronger than everyone there.  Her youth brought a headstrong attitude and she was much more extreme in her methods than the others.  Believing her sisters to not be giving their all to thweir cause, Ash left the nunery and took off into the world to make it a better place.  At a local tavern, she met up with a man, by the name of Luis Sangre.  She heard his tragic story and agreed to accompany him on his quest for moral support.

units.caption: A PURE tag team of Luis Cesar Sangre and Sister Ash Maximoff, billed together as Luis Sangre & Ashley Maximoff and finishing with 1: Hellfire and Brimstone 2: Baño Sangre (Luis's) 3: Faith (Ash's).

units.name: Monsters Inc.

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-11-p339-360.html.

units.caption: Abyss and Goliath, who take the tag belts from the Blue World Order at Guilty As Charged with a Double Chokeslam and keep them on Revolution against the Dudley Boys with the Iron Saints' help. In February and March 2007 Abyss and Goliath stay with Raven, who demands a tag title shot for his 'monsters' and is refused by Shane Douglas; at Baptism Of Fire Goliath is the first man eliminated from the Baptism Of Fire match, pushed into the flames by eight others, and Abyss is thrown over by Sabu and Tommy Dreamer. In April 2007 Monsters Inc help CM Punk beat Lance Storm and beat the Iron Saints on Revolution; in May they hold Kelly Thomaselli for Raven and, at Hardcore Heaven, are beaten by the Iron Saints, an upset, before chokeslamming them in a second attack with Vito. In June they beat Team England's Nigel McGuinness with a Double Chokeslam and lose to Paul Burchill and Davey Boy Smith. At Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 Goliath is found laid out in the car park and Abyss loses to Paul Burchill's Release German Suplex through tables; in July they lose to Mark Calaway (a Chokeslam on Abyss) and, in the handicap match Raven books against Vito, Vito wins with Calaway's help, and at Summer Assylum they lose to the Iron Saints in the six-man tag with CM Punk; in August Vito beats Goliath with a Shining Wizard. On Blood, Sweat and Beers in August 2007 Vito Thomaselli beats them with Shane Douglas's help; at Heatwave Goliath carries a key to the cage door of the Barbed Wire Cage Match so that they can enter, and Vito drives them out with a Double DDT; in September they stand by Raven and CM Punk, hitting Vito and Burchill with Double Chokeslams. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Abyss's Big Boot hits CM Punk by mistake and Vito Thomaselli's springboard somersault plancha takes both monsters down; in October they stand by Punk, and at Guilty As Charged they hold Vito for Punk's chair shots in the Last Man Standing Match (a Black Hole Slam by Abyss, a Chokeslam by Goliath) until the referee stops it. In November 2007 Abyss and Goliath interfere for Raven's Nest in the main events on Revolution, where Shane Douglas fights them off with a chair and Chris Jericho clears them with another; Abyss taps to Jericho's Liontamer in the six-man tag on Blood, Sweat and Beers. At November To Remember XV Abyss and Goliath escort the champion Raven to the ring and stand in front of his corner for the Loser Leaves ECW Match. On the Saturday show they beat down Paul Burchill with Raven's Nest until Sabu and The Sandman, in 'ECW Enforcer' shirts, clear Abyss and Goliath; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Abyss flattens Vito Thomaselli with a Black Hole Slam and Sabu chairs him out of the ring.

tenures.finisher: Termination — Josh applies a boston crab whilst Johnny locks on a crippler crossface as Ric comes of the top rope with a moonsault to the exposed back
tenures.bio:
Born in the same neighbourhood, their mothers were and still are 

good friends. at first Ric and Johnny could not stand the sight of each 

other. With both of the two trying to out do each other wether it be with 

the females or in sport. 



This carried on untill Ric's very first day of high school. Johnny was 

already at High school as he was two years older then Ric. Ric at the time 

was a very shy individual, and did not associate well with the other kids. 

Two of the schools bullies took note of Rics coyness and decided to take 

advantage of it. Upon seeing this Johnny went flipmode and completely 

kicked the two bullies asses. After Ric asked why Johnny did what he did, but 

Johnny has not mentioned why till this very day. 



The two of them stuck together like glue from that day onwards. Johnny 

always had Ric's back and vice verser. They realised that they could not 

live up to their fathers standard (who were successful businessmen). So they 

decided to join a local gym and become established athletes but in what 

sport? Johnny had the braun and an animal like mentality. While on the 

other hand Ric was a swift and cunning little S.O.B! One day they was 

working out, when Ric noticed a poster on the wall: Who's tougher then you.

units.name: Raven's Nest

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-02-p638-649.html.

units.caption: Raven's own stable, announced as the 'newly re-formed Raven's Nest' on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of February 2007, when Raven beats Sabu for the World Heavyweight Championship with Paul Burchill and Goliath's help, throws Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through the ringside tables ('time to take out the trash') and is joined by Abyss, Vito and CM Punk. In March Raven demands a tag title shot for his 'monsters' and is refused by Shane Douglas, beats Douglas at Baptism Of Fire with Punk's help to become the Revolution commissioner, and sees Paul Burchill win the Baptism Of Fire match for the Nest. In April 2007 Raven, as commissioner, fires Owen Hart, and the Nest, with the Canadian Connection's help, unmask the masked man who has been attacking them, who turns out to be Vito, while a voice on the PA says it will not be that easy; at Cyberslam Raven keeps the World Heavyweight Championship over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match with Paul Burchill as special referee, and Burchill then turns on Raven with a C-4 and leaves the Nest: on the next Blood, Sweat and Beers Burchill and Shane Douglas, the real masked man, tell how the plan ran for seven months. In May the Nest (Raven, CM Punk, Abyss, Goliath and Vito) take Kelly Thomaselli, Vito's sister, as a hostage against Burchill, and at Hardcore Heaven Raven beats Burchill when Punk threatens to throw Kelly off the stage and then does; in June the Nest face Burchill, Shane Douglas, Team England and Davey Boy Smith. In June 2007 Raven has Paul Heyman clear the arena so that the Nest can face Paul Burchill alone and beats him down with a run of finishers, then collapses when a chanting video plays; on Revolution he admits he commissioned the videos and hijacked ecw.com himself, until the Iron Saints, out of hospital, wreck the Nest with chairs. At Wrestlepalooza Vito turns on CM Punk and the Saints leave Punk and Abyss on the girders under the stage, Burchill beats Abyss, and Raven keeps the World Heavyweight Championship over both Harts and is Chokeslammed by the mystery signing, Mark Calaway. In July Calaway and Vito beat Raven and Punk and Monsters Inc, Raven turns Vito's First Blood Match into a pinfall match, shocks Calaway and Vito with cattle prods and sends the Nest after Calaway and the Saints, a Heyman eight-man tag ends in a no contest, and at Summer Assylum the Iron Saints beat Punk and Monsters Inc, Vito powerbombing Punk through a table, before Raven keeps his title over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway. In August Goliath loses to Vito and Raven tells him he cannot face Vito at Heatwave. In August 2007 the Nest run in on the mass brawl and on Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas; at Heatwave Raven's cage stipulation, Monsters Inc.'s key and CM Punk's GTS on Vito Thomaselli after Burchill's top-of-the-cage Corkscrew Cross Body let Raven keep the World Heavyweight Championship, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers he reads out clause 17.2a of the contract, which voids a title change after outside interference, and uses clause 24.17e, as Commissioner, to hold Burchill's and Douglas's contracts over them. In September Raven brings in Alexis Laree, 'the cream of the CZW crop', Punk keeps the International All Action Championship, Raven hits Burchill with the Raven Effect after his wins, and Raven is booked to defend against Rhino at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Nate Hatred beats Paul Burchill and Burchill is fired, Raven pins Rhino after Mark Calaway's Chokeslam and is then chokeslammed by Calaway. In October Owen Hart makes Raven tap on Revolution, Raven loses a cage match to Chris Jericho and is chokeslammed by Calaway; at Guilty As Charged Raven, as Commissioner, books his own match, pins Jericho with a Raven Effect and becomes seven-time champion, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers the company's owner returns, strips him of his powers as Commissioner, gives booking power back to Paul Heyman and books Paul Burchill against him for November To Remember XV. Alexis Laree wins the first Lioness Championship, and Nattie Neidhart joins the Nest as 'the anonymous blonde'. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as their champion, has CM Punk stripped of the International All Action Championship by security guards, and says that Paul Burchill will beat Raven at November To Remember; the whole Nest assaults Burchill on the second Revolution until Chris Jericho's chair shots and a C-4 turn it, and Raven is left alone in the ring. Alexis Laree and Nathalie work together against Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli, and on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Heyman makes Raven's match a Loser Leaves ECW Match. At November To Remember XV Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill and is out of ECW; CM Punk, Alexis Laree and the others lose their leader. On the Saturday show Punk tells Burchill, Vito Thomaselli and Shane Douglas that Raven 'ensured that I was ready to take his place as the leader of the Nest' and loses to Burchill with a C-4; the Nest's run-in is cleared by the ECW Enforcers. Punk and Goliath lose on Revolution on the first Monday of December to Burchill and Vito Thomaselli by disqualification, when Punk low-blows Vito.

units.caption: The two masked newcomers of The Fallen who work as a tag team: they lose to Smith and Singh at Summer Showdown in June 2010, beat Grayson & Shaffer at Iron in August, trading masks to confuse the referee, lose a three-way for the Tag Team titles to Valentine & Johnson at Back To School and take part in the Eleventh Hour match in November 2010 where, unmasked as Marc Speed and Greg Ford, they make their "debut" as Ford & Speed against Morgan & Benning and win with a Cross Armbreaker. As Ford & Speed they beat the Bailey Boys at Remember November in November 2010, lose to Morgan & Benning at End Of Days, beat Smith & Singh at All Or Nothing in February 2011, lose to Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson at Leap Into The Unknown and beat the Young Americans at April Showers. As Ford & Speed they tell the crowd on 12th May 2011 that they are no longer associated with The Fallen but follow its ideals, beat Stevie Grayson and Thomas Morgan that night, are beaten in the Hotter Than Hot three-way, and beat Smith & Singh at Summernova and the West Texas Peacekeepers at Iron with Fallen Chances. As Ford & Speed they beat the West Texas Peacekeepers at Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011 with Fallen Chances, lose to Team OMGsplosion at Eleventh Hour, lose the Tag Team title three-way at Season's Beatings and the title match to Smith & Singh at End Of Days, and beat the Young Americans, Callum and Raphael on 5th January 2012 to earn a shot at the Invitational, where they lose the three-way with Smith & Singh and Lockdown. As Ford & Speed they beat Amazing Fire Fly and Jared Johnson at All Or Nothing on 12th February 2012 and the West Texas Peacekeepers at March Madness, and are in the Spring Fever three-way. As Ford & Speed in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 they lose the three-way at High Noon on 5th June, beat Kid Arachnid and Bradford Peverell at South East Madness, the West Texas Peacekeepers at Summernova and Smith & Singh at Back To School with Fallen Chances, the narrator saying they have lacked direction since being set loose from The Fallen.

tenures.source: /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-march-to-hell-2004-10-21.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-march-to-hell-ii-2004-10-28.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-holiday-havoc-i-2004-11-19.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-holiday-havoc-ii-2004-12-03.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-new-years-kick-off-2005-01-19.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-road-to-rhyolite-2005-01-27.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-march-to-madness-results-2005-03-02.html; /promotions/vwf-vegas-2003/archive/vwf-the-gauntlet-2005-2005-04-11.html
tenures.note: Named as a four-man group on March To Hell (21 October 2004), interfering to help Sebastian and G-Gangsta against Capsman and Evil Capsman, then unable to save Iyasu Saku from Adam Jennings's own VWF 24 Hour Championship defense. Loses members to individual matches on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) -- G-Gangsta to Fast Eddie Cutlass, Robbie Caldwell to Randall Crane, Iyasu Saku to Classy Joey Boy -- and offers a fourth membership slot to Classy Joey Boy, who turns on Sebastian, G-Gangsta and Caldwell instead. Beats down stablemate Iyasu Saku in an apparent staged play on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), the returning Rodeo Boys jumping Paddy O'Shea afterward and, by the broadcast's own account, joining the group; loses the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse elimination match's own final fall to Sebastian, the last man standing, and Robbie Caldwell loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Adam Jennings the same night. Enters the tag team title battle royal five men strong on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), eliminated one by one until only Sebastian remains, beaten by mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov. G-Gangsta fails to appear for a six-man tag on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), instead returning after the bell to beat down Sebastian and publicly resign from the group. Runs in on former member G-Gangsta -- teamed with Fast Eddie Cutlass against Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov -- on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), Sebastian, Robbie Caldwell and the Rodeo Boys stretchering him out of the building. Now four strong with Robbie Caldwell, Kenny Kidd, Billy Bones and the debuting Mad Bomber, sweeping March To Madness (2 March 2005): Caldwell beats Thunder Valenkov after Kidd distracts the referee and the Mad Bomber blinds Valenkov with a smoke bomb and chairs him, Kidd beats Fast Eddie Cutlass, and the debuting Mad Bomber beats Lark Fenriz. Demands matches for Billy Bones and The Mad Bomber from John Tyler backstage at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005); enters the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal with only Robbie Caldwell representing the group, Kenny Kidd having already been eliminated from the eight-man elimination match earlier on the same card and Billy Bones and The Mad Bomber never entering the battle royal at all.

tenures.note: Loses the VWF Tag Team Championship to Hot Property in a Flashback ambush on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then wins the Dog Day One tag team battle royal. Loses the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round to Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone, then is beaten down by Hot Property and Flash in a special Flashback before competing in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), Kenny Kidd falling from the ladder alongside Stevie Knight. Reported gone for good after Billy Bones's own contract release on Wrestle Style V.3, the pair are reinstated to the VWF on the spot at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) after lawyer RAR intervenes with majority owner Kingston Cash, then immediately beat down new VWF Tag Team Champions Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen with cowbells. Loses a VWF Tag Team Championship match by disqualification after Kenny Kidd brands Marcus O'Malley on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Loses the title rematch to a substitute Outlaw Morris Bass and Mark McQueen on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), Billy Bones submitting to the Devils Snare. Wins a weapons-advantage Number One Contenders match over The Mighty Men at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Bones branding The Reckoning's face and pinning The Salvation. Interferes to help the Riders of the Apocalypse beat down Iyasu Saku and jump Paddy O'Shea on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), read by the broadcast's own commentary as the pair joining the group; helps eliminate Capsman first in the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse match before both members are eliminated themselves. Both eliminated separately from the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), Kenny Kidd by mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov and Billy Bones by a returning Sonicman. Billy Bones loses to Sonicman on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005); the pair works over The Reckoning's ankle together during Kenny Kidd's own title-feud win the same night.

tenures.note: Mark McQueen and Marcus O'Malley beat Blaze and The Real Deal on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then compete in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, eliminated in a mutual elimination with Orion; leader Kevin Simmons announces his own in-character retirement the same Firestorm broadcast. Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen win the sixteen-man Dog Days 3 tag scramble together on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), O'Malley unhooking the suspended ring; O'Malley alone had wrestled the Dog Day Two tag bracket for the team the week before, McQueen barred from competing. Billed a Society of Doom member in his own Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) ring introduction, Adam Jennings wins the VWF 24 Hour Championship from Kevin Blair; The Outlaw Morris Bass runs in alongside Jennings, O'Malley and McQueen, all named on commentary as the Society of Doom, to save Kevin Simmons from a Kingston Cash chair attack during the night's own ladder match. Kevin Simmons and Outlaw Morris Bass win by disqualification over The Mighty Men on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen chase off a backstage beatdown of Simmons on March To Hell II (28 October 2004). All four -- Simmons, O'Malley, McQueen and Adam Jennings -- enter the Rage in the Cage together as the Society of Doom at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Simmons pinning O'Malley to become the new co-holder of the VWF Tag Team Championship. Adam Jennings and Mark McQueen, both billed members, help fight off the Riders of the Apocalypse in a post-match brawl after Jennings retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Kevin Simmons and Marcus O'Malley are confirmed suspended from the VWF by New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), leaving only Jennings and McQueen active.

Havoc's own membership was confirmed when he and Crimestarter Jim beat the Big Shots in the World Tag Team Title Tournament's first round, managed by Monique and Kim (28 June 1998); the same broadcast showed further associates "Playboy" Jude St. Claire and Black Diamond ambushing two number-one-contender hopefuls on the stable's behalf, and bodyguard Romulus escorting the group. tenures.bio: (sorry its crappy) Originally from Osaka, Japan, Ryu and Otoshi have been lifelong friends and have always had a passion for Professional wrestler, gaining a small following in Japan, the two decided to go over to America thinking they could make it there,they joined up with PWA a local training acadamy and after they proved themselves they were released from there. Ryu and Otoshi soon became champions of numerous feds mainly with the indy fed NTICW in which they got involved in a cult called the Followers of the hidden star, after the closure of NTICW, the sushi crew (as they were called) joined up with global sensation PCW, but quit after one week deciding wrestling wasn't fun anymore, a couple of months past until PURE owner Jamar came to the sushi crew with an offer to join PURE, seeing this as an oppurtunity to go back to their homeland the sushi crew accepted and went back to Japan, after 2 shows the Sushi crew with the help of their unwanted partner Shaun Styles won the Trinity belts which they still hold on today...

units.caption: A PURE tag team of Ryu Sotosucki and Otoshi Mishimoto, billed together as Sushi Crew and finishing with Raw Sushi.

Challenged the Bod Squad (Tara "Sunburst" Marshall and Brianna Landis) for the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship on 8 September 2004 and lost by disqualification after Marshall drove a chair into Ishikawa's spine to save Landis from a spike piledriver; the title stayed with the champions. Teamed with Sierra Browne to beat Donna Tetreault and the Bod Squad in a non-title six-woman tag on 2 October 2004, Sierra Browne's own Truth Superkick finishing Brianna Landis for the pin. Reona Yoshida departed the UWF for Joshi Puroresu STARDOM by 11 June 2005; Misaki Ishikawa continued the pairing's own Women's Tag Team Championship reign under a new name, the Psychommunity, with older sister Naomi Ishikawa as her new partner.

tenures.note: Debuts by inserting itself into a VWF Tag Team Championship match already underway between champions Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov and challengers Frank O'Shea and Billy Bones at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), Simon Davidson pinning O'Shea to win the titles after Justin Davidson pulls Valenkov from the ring to stop a cover. Retains the titles by disqualification against McQueen and Valenkov at End Of March (30 March 2005) after the returning Hot Property run in on McQueen; a legal challenge filed the same night argues the team was never a signed, named participant in the St Patricks Day match and so could not legitimately win the championship, left for the VWF's incoming ownership to decide. Defends the titles, billed with a question mark over its own legitimacy, against a returning Henry Fish (billed Scott Starring) and an unidentified stand-in wrestling as the absent Van Wild at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), winning by pinfall; the team's own hired ring announcer, not the broadcast's regular ring announcer, declares the team champions afterward.

Won gauntlet falls over the Rodeo Boys, Purgatory and Team Essington at Fear Is Coming III before losing to Marcus O'Malley and Kagedo, then lost a three-way tag to Tap Out City alongside Purgatory at Phear Phantastic 2005. Fought the Rodeo Boys to a no-contest on Winter War III after Team Essington's own four-man run-in, earning a spot in a fatal four-way for the VXW Tag Team Championship at Ghost Town Blues.

units.caption: The England squad for ECW's Wrestling World Cup in July 2007, announced in June 2007: Steven Regal, released from his Federation contract, introduces himself as its active team captain and recruits Paul Burchill, who agrees, and the developmental talents Nigel McGuinness and Doug Williams. Williams and McGuinness come out with steel chairs to even the numbers against Raven's Nest on Revolution, lose to CM Punk and Vito on Blood, Sweat and Beers and, after a no contest on Burchill's match, lose again to Vito and Monsters Inc on the next Revolution. In the World Cup of July 2007 England win the first Pool B match, over India, lose to Mexico twice and to India once (Raven and Punk distract Paul Burchill), and scrape into the quarter-finals one point ahead of India; they beat Team USA when Burchill beats Jay Briscoe, Christopher Daniels and Jerry Lynn after Kurt Angle's punch, beat Mexico when Burchill beats Rey Mysterio Jr. and Eddie Guerrero with a Double C-4, and win the first Wrestling World Cup at Summer Assylum when Burchill, last of the three left, beats Masato Tanaka, Jushin Lyger and Ultimo Dragon; Paul Heyman presents the trophy. Davey Boy Smith is on the squad throughout.

Lost a gauntlet fall to Team Brittania at Fear Is Coming III (their own final match together); released from Essington Sports Inc soon after and replaced under the same team name by a wholly new pairing, a seven-foot Mr. Smith and a four-foot Mr. Jones, who lost a debut match to the Rodeo Boys by disqualification at Phear Phantastic 2005. Beat a debuting masked lucha team, Los Diablos, on Winter War II, then ran in as a four-man unit, fielding a newly introduced fourth member, Mr. Sal, to break up a Rodeo Boys/Team Brittania match on Winter War III and demand a VXW Tag Team Championship shot.

In October 2007 Arsenal drops Sam Strong through his own desk with a C4 Suplex, and the team beats Veteran Mentality three times, the last at A Haunting in America. In November 2007 Arsenal and Ota side with Seduction against Triple D, who leaves her tied to a chair in the Masked Man's video to finish a match; they lose the tag belts to The Valentines at Pilgrimage when Devine turns on Arsenal, and Arsenal takes Devine to over twenty minutes on the Monday of Week 3. units.caption: A comic stable that returns to Revolution in September 2006 and sets about pranking Charlie Pag, Paul Burchill and Raven before Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova win the tag belts. In February 2007 Big Stevie Cool beats The Great Sasuke at Living Dangerously with a Stevie Kick that catches him in mid-air; in March the Sasuke World Order drag Big Stevie Cool, Hollywood Nova and Da Blue Guy under the ring, and at Baptism Of Fire Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova turn on Da Blue Guy and kneel with the cult to worship The Great Sasuke. In June 2007 Al Snow and Big Stevie Cool pair up against Rhino, Stevie superkicking Rhino through a table at Wrestlepalooza and Snow thanking him for it afterwards with the mannequin head; on Revolution in July Snow is named a new member, 'BW Snow', and Head 'Head of Bluecurity'. The bWo spray-paint Rhino, are beaten 4-on-1 on Revolution, Stevie Kicks the sWo and sprays 'bWo' on every one of them, lose to the Dudley Boyz in the first defence of the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles when the sWo's Chessman and Oz hit them with the belts, and prank Oz by hanging the sWo's sign on the ladies' locker room. In August 2007 the bWo take BW Snow to the ring ('WE WANT HEAD'), are floored by Espiritu and Escoria, and beat the sWo with a Stevie Kick on Oz on Revolution; at Heatwave Big Stevie Cool loses to Big Sasuke Cool when six Sasukes emerge from under the ring. In September the bWo beat the sWo when Hollywood Nova, disguised as Chessman, turns on them, beat Oz on Blood, Sweat and Beers and beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz on F' The Mainstream; Big Stevie Cool and Big Sasuke Cool meet again at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Big Stevie Cool loses to Big Sasuke Cool; in October the bWo beat the sWo on Revolution with a Stevie Kick on Chessman, free BW Snow with Big Stevie Cool in a Sasuke mask, and lose the next match when the 'mole' (who proves to be Big Stevie Cool) attacks them from under the ring. At Guilty As Charged Big Stevie Cool turns on Hollywood Nova and BW Snow with Stevie Kicks and leaves with Sasuke; the diary's Bam Bam Exam reports ECW releasing the Blue Meanie.
