units.caption: The tag champions Oscar Golden and Flash Savage and their ninja-obsessed partner Hugh Lee, who hold the MAW Tag Team titles until the Beach Blast ladder match. They beat the Bailey Boys at Summernova in August 2010, win the Tag Team titles for a record third time at Fall Of The King in September, and keep them in a four-team ladder match at Where It All Begins Again in October and against Brandon Smith and Joe Benning on a November tour show. They keep the Tag Team titles at Remember November in November 2010 and Season's Beatings, spike-piledrive Brandon Smith after End Of Days, lose the belts to Cattley and Singh at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, beat Smith & Singh at the Invitational and the Internet Favourites at All Or Nothing and lose a rematch to Cattley and Singh at Third Time's The Charm, where Oscar Golden flirts with a girl at ringside. They beat Cattley & Singh for the Tag Team titles at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, are brought home drunk by two policemen who are MAW fans, boast on 12th June of being four-time champions, debut the O, Canada! at Summer Showdown and keep the belts through the summer; at Back To School Raphael joins them in a six-man loss to Smith, Singh and Ota. They keep the Tag Team titles against the Young Americans and Smith & Singh on 26th September 2011 and on the 3rd and 24th October tour shows, lose them to Smith & Singh at Where It All Begins Again, beat the West Texas Peacekeepers at Season's Beatings, Peverell and McManus at End Of Days and the Internet Favourites on 5th January 2012, when Kristen Pearce joins them, and say that they have never had their rematch. At Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March 2012, in the Asylum in Michigan, they cash in their rematch four months after dropping the Tag Team titles and lose to Smith & Singh; they lose to KC Glenn and Jared Johnson at Third Time's The Charm and are in the four-team match at April Showers. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 they lose the three-way debut of Always Breakin' Hollywood at High Noon on 5th June, beat Spectrum Infinity with O, Canada! at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, lose to them at Summernova on 5th August with Kristen Pearce at their side, and beat Smith & Singh at South East Grand Parade on 9th August.

units.name: The Canadian Connection

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-12-p434-506.html.

units.caption: Chris Jericho, Christian and Chris Benoit, who join forces at November To Remember after Benoit and Eddie Guerrero fight to a draw, take the name on Revolution in December 2006 and preach the superiority of Canada, and feud with Eddie Guerrero, Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera (Team Mexico), against whom they win the six-man tag at Got Blood?. In February 2007 the group beat Team Mexico in the Lucha Libre six-man tag at Living Dangerously with Christian's Unprettier on Juventud Guerrera, and win the three-way Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire against Team Mexico and Team JAPAN, when Chris Benoit, the last man in, eliminates Jushin Lyger, Ultimo Dragon, Eddie Guerrero and Juventud Guerrera with the Crossface and a Diving Headbutt; Christian attacks the Whole F**kin' Show with brass knuckles after the pay-per-view, and in April the group beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick and take the ECW World Television Championship when Chris Jericho pins Bret Hart in the Triangle Match. In April 2007 the Canadian Connection beat the Iron Saints, take Raven's deal to jump the masked man and, at Cyberslam, win the three-way dance for the number one contendership to the World Tag Team Championship over Los Guerreros and the Dudley Boys, while Chris Jericho loses the Television Championship to Rob Van Dam. In May they beat Lyger and Ultimo Dragon, ally with AJ Styles and Chris Hero, lose the tag title match at Hardcore Heaven when Shawn Michaels pins Christian, and help AJ Styles take the Television Championship with hockey sticks; in June Don Callis coaches Team Canada, with Lance Storm, Chris Benoit, Christian, Chris Jericho, Teddy Hart and Bobby Roode. In July 2007 Jericho, Christian and Benoit play for Team Canada in the World Cup. By the end of that month the diary reports that Christian has signed with the WWA and left ECW; in August Jericho forces Benoit to tap to the Walls Of Jericho on Revolution, and Owen Hart, whom Jericho mocks as an old-timer, challenges him to a match at Heatwave.

units.name: The Cult of Sasuke

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-09-p195-231.html.

units.caption: A masked Super Juniors cult led by The Great Sasuke, who arrives on F' The Mainstream in September 2006 with five disciples vowing mayhem, strips the Iron Saints and the Dudley Boys to their underwear, stages ritual assaults on LA Park and Jushin Lyger, and wins LA Park for the group at Anarchy Rulz. In December 2006 The Great Sasuke renames the group the Sasuke World Order and announces that it will take over F' The Mainstream and then the world. In February 2007 the group, now the Sasuke World Order, tear off their shirts to show sWo logos spray-painted on their chests and The Great Sasuke loses to Big Stevie Cool at Living Dangerously; in March the cult drag Big Stevie Cool, Hollywood Nova and Da Blue Guy under the ring, and at Baptism Of Fire Stevie and Nova, now under Sasuke's spell, turn on Da Blue Guy and kneel to worship him. In April the Dudley Boys, as the self-styled enforcers of ECW, take on the cult, and Sasuke hangs life-size mannequins of the Dudleys from the rafters. In June 2007 the Sasuke World Order storm the ring on Revolution to claim a place as a twelfth World Cup team; in the pool stage they lose to Team USA twice, lose once to Italy when Oz's chair swing backfires and win once by swapping masks, and, with Cuervo's spray paint costing Italy its last match against Team USA, qualify by a single bonus point; they beat Samoa in the quarter-final with Oz's distraction, Cuervo's 2x4 and Sasuke's wits. They lose the semi-final to Japan when Tajiri, in Sasuke's mask, pins Chessman; after the tournament Sasuke beats Tajiri with Oz's lead pipe and the sWo paint the ECW flag, until two Chessmen and Big Stevie Cool's bWo invade and spray 'bWo' on the sWo, and in August Oz, tricked by the bWo into the ladies' locker room, is Super Kicked by Shawn Michaels. In August 2007 the sWo take on Espiritu and Escoria, who argue over 'We're overtaking' and 'We're taking over', brawl with the bWo on Revolution and lose to them before Heatwave, where Big Sasuke Cool beats Big Stevie Cool by hiding five extra Sasukes under the ring and a Michinoku Driver. In September Hollywood Nova, painted as Chessman, tricks the sWo, Sasuke pins Nova with a school boy, Oz is pinned by a Stevie Kick, Sasuke loses the International All Action Title Match to CM Punk when Monsters Inc. interfere, and Chris Hero pins Sasuke on F' The Mainstream. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Big Sasuke Cool beats Big Stevie Cool with a Michinoku Driver after a low blow, as Chessman and four men dressed as Hollywood Nova run in. In October the sWo take BW Snow hostage and show him a Kevin Nash and John Cena match, are tricked when the bWo send Big Stevie Cool in as a masked 'Sasuke' to free him and show the real Sasuke 'The Best of Monday Night Raw', and lose on Blood, Sweat and Beers when a masked 'mole' attacks the bWo's men from under the ring. At Guilty As Charged, with the loser to disband, Big Sasuke Cool pins Hollywood Nova, Superkicks Chessman and leaves with Big Stevie Cool as the True World Order; the diary's Bam Bam Exam then lists Chessman, Cuervo, Escoria, Espiritu and Oz among the workers ECW is releasing.

The id is unchanged, so every reference still resolves and no alias is owed. STILL OPEN, and deliberately not touched here: the extraction wired this unit row into two CSWA shows' match sides (SUPERPRIMETIME: I HAVE A DREAM, 15 January 1996; CSWA ANNIVERSARY 1996, 31 March 1996) and the two members individually into nine others, so the same team is sometimes one entity and sometimes two. units.caption: Firebird and Black Eagle, billed as The Dark Raptors in a three-way for the Tag Team titles against Smith & Singh and the Canadian Blondes at Mother, May I? on 26th May 2011, where Oscar Golden crotches Firebird on the top rope and the Blondes retain. As Firebird and Black Eagle they lose to Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson at Spring Fever; after the three-way they stand with JD Morgan and the converted Masked Patriot, presented as Providence, as the four men who "have something greater". They beat the Young Americans at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011, where Firebird announces that they are the champions-elect, lose the Tag Team title three-way at Season's Beatings when Singh pins Firebird, and beat Lassana Makutsi and Amazing Fire Fly at End Of Days. They lose to KC Glenn and Randy Bumfhole at All Or Nothing on 12th February 2012, when Bumfhole pins Black Eagle; Eagle's spinal surgery that follows leaves Firebird on a singles run and the tag division with more heel teams than face ones. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 Firebird and Black Eagle win the Tag Team titles from Smith & Singh at Summer Showdown on 12th June as part of The Fallen, keep them against the West Texas Peacekeepers on 9th July, the XX Factor on 5th August and Spectrum Infinity on 12th August, and lose them to Team Honor at Back To School on 5th September, when Eagle taps out.

units.name: The Dudley Boys

tenures.source: The diary's own shows bill the team on 3 of its first ten shows, from /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/show-001-p17-21.html.

units.caption: The tag team that holds the ECW World Tag Team Championship through the diary's first ten shows, beating the Hardy Boys for it on the first and eighth. In March and April 2007 the Dudley Boys, billed as the enforcers of ECW, beat The Sandman on Blood, Sweat and Beers at Tommy Dreamer's booking, are eliminated together by Rhino at Baptism Of Fire, and beat Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova with 3Ds on Blood, Sweat and Beers and Revolution while the Sasuke World Order hunt them. At Cyberslam in April 2007 the Dudley Boys take out Los Guerreros with 3Ds and a Spike Powerbomb through tables in the three-way dance for the tag number one contendership, but the Canadian Connection run in and pin them both; in May D-Von pins Chavo Guerrero Jr. with a 3D. The Dudley Boys return at Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 to attack the Whole F**kin' Show, and in July beat the Hardcore Innovators for the number one contendership with the help of Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Daizy, whom they introduce on Revolution as the children of their missing brother Big Dick Dudley. They lose the Tables Match for the World Tag Team Championship at Summer Assylum, then rename the old World Tag Team belts the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, keep them over the bWo with the sWo's interference and over Balls & Axl, and are challenged by the Innovators and Los Guerreros. In August 2007 they keep the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles over Los Guerreros (a 3D on Chavo) on Revolution, over the Samoan Gangstas (a 3D on Anoai) on Blood, Sweat and Beers and over the Briscoe Boys in their last defence before Heatwave, all with their relatives' help, and the Hardcore Innovators then cane the second generation, DDT the two of them and walk off with the belts; at Heatwave Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer put D-Von through a table with a Double DDT and win the titles. In September they lose a tag title match to the Whole F**kin' Show on Revolution when simultaneous finishers beat Bubba Ray and D-Von, D-Von is pinned by Shawn Michaels's Super Kick despite interference from Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II, Bubba Ray pins Michaels with a 3D in a non-title match, and the mystery Dudley, Slyk Tayshaun, attacks them both. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the second generation of Dudleyz break up the Champions versus Champions match, Bubba Ray and D-Von put the Hardcore Innovators down with a 3D, and the Dudleyz take both sets of tag belts from ringside; D-Von beats Tommy Dreamer on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and on the first Revolution of October Shawn Michaels pins Bubba Ray with a Super Kick. Paul Heyman books the Three Way Dance for the tag titles at Guilty As Charged, and there the Dudley Boyz pin Rob Van Dam after Michaels's Super Kick takes him down and win the unified belts, which the Hardcore Innovators carry out of the arena. In November 2007 Bubba Ray and D-Von, standing with the Dudley Family, challenge the Hardcore Innovators, who walk around with all four tag belts, to a title match at November To Remember XV; Slyk Tayshaun Dudley then chairs the Dudley Family and the two of them, and D-Von tells him that he is fouling his own doorstep. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match in which the Dudley Boyz and the Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills it with the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (30 November 2007 in the diary's history) Bubba Ray and D-Von, with Big Dick Jr., Ultimo Dudley II and Daizy, beat the Hardcore Innovators in a weapons match: D-Von lifts Beulah McGillicutty for Bubba's Superbomb through a table, and a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table pins Tommy Dreamer; they raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles, and Slyk Tayshaun Dudley then comes to the ring with a baseball bat and beats down every one of his relatives. On Revolution on the first Monday of December they defend the Undisputed belts against the Thomaselli brothers, the match is restarted as a Three Way Dance with Slyk and Dick Jr., and Slyk breaks up Bubba's pin on Brandon and makes Bubba tap to the Boston Crabs. The diary's next preview bills them as the 'Original Dudleyz'; on Saturday, with Ultimo Dudley II, they chair and powerbomb the Thomasellis through a table after the new champions' first defence.

units.name: The Dudley Family

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-07-p1065-1139.html.

units.caption: The 'first family of Dudleyville': Bubba Ray and D-Von Dudley, who introduce their 'second generation' on Revolution in July 2007, Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Daizy Dudley, the 'nephew' and 'niece' of the Dudley Boyz and children of the missing Big Dick Dudley, and at Summer Assylum a third, Ultimo Dudley II. With the second generation at ringside the Dudleys win the number one contendership, lose the Tables Match at Summer Assylum to the Whole F**kin' Show, rename the old World Tag Team belts the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, and defend them against the bWo, Balls & Axl and, on the previews, Los Guerreros and the Hardcore Innovators. In August 2007 the family (Bubba Ray, D-Von, Daizy, Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II) interfere in the Dudleyz's title defences and lose a match to the Hardcore Innovators on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Ultimo Dudley II is pinned after a Double DDT; at Heatwave they tell the Innovators in a backstage promo the story of Big Daddy Dudley's grizzly bear and the table, before the Dudleyz lose the belts. In September they beat the Briscoe Boys, the F.B.I. and the Headhunters on F' The Mainstream and lose to the bWo, Daizy beats Traci in a catfight match when Big Dick Jr. hits her with a Total Penetration Chokebomb, Kelly Thomaselli beats Daizy to qualify for the Lioness' Den, and an unnamed Dudley, Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, a son of Big Dick Dudley, attacks the family with a chair and a flagpole, saying D-Von knows a secret that made his father leave, until the family beat him and put him through a table. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the family run in on the Champions versus Champions match and carry off both sets of belts. In October they ask Paul Heyman for a Flaming Tables Match, Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II lose to the Whole F**kin' Show and to the Hardcore Innovators (Dreamer's DDT on Ultimo Dudley II), Big Dick Jr. is pinned by Shawn Michaels and by Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, who kicks him low after calling out 'is that Big Dick?', and at Guilty As Charged they help the Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance before the Innovators leave them laid out backstage and take the belts. In November 2007 Daizy tells the Hardcore Innovators that the belts they carry belong to her uncles, and the family run out to the Innovators after they beat the Thomaselli brothers, until Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, a cousin who calls them a disgrace, chairs Daizy, Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II and then Bubba Ray and D-Von, and says that he is entering the International All Action Title Tournament and means to find out the secret his father kept. He beats Scorpio Sky after the Second Generation run in and are chaired, clears the family again when the Second Generation lose to the Innovators with a Double DDT on Revolution, and on the last Revolution before the pay-per-view takes a five-on-one beating from the whole family until the Innovators arrive with Singapore canes. At November To Remember XV Big Dick Jr. costs his cousin Slyk Tayshaun Dudley the International All Action Championship with a Total Penetration, and Daizy and D-Von tell the camera that the family will 'take out the Hardcore Innovators'; Slyk then batters every one of his relatives, even Daizy, with a baseball bat and says that he will find out the secret about his father. On the Saturday show Ultimo Dudley II trips Slyk into Dick Jr.'s Total Penetration through a table, and Dick wins the falls-count-anywhere match. On Revolution on the first Monday of December Slyk interrupts his uncles' title defence with the bat, Dick Jr. blocks it with a chair, and in the restarted Three Way Dance Slyk and Dick Jr. win the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; on Saturday Slyk, in a backstage scene, asks Dick Jr. and Daizy to join him in finding the family secret, with the belts as leverage, and the new champions beat the Thomasellis with Daizy's help before the Original Dudleyz (Bubba Ray, D-Von and Ultimo Dudley II) destroy the brothers.

units.notes: The Outlaw's stable. In December 1997 it is the Outlaw, the Executive and Steel Cold: on 12 December the Outlaw and the Executive bring Steel Cold a briefcase with his name on it (the booth argues it out: "We have no proof Steel is part of their group." / "His name was on the briefcase.", wwa-1997-12-12); on 19 December the card bills the Outlaw "a part of the Executive's Club", the Outlaw says "Steel Cold and I will be watching", and when Steel Cold comes out alone the booth asks "is there a problem in the Executive Club already?" (wwa-1997-12-19). On 2 January 1998 Steel Cold is written out (an in-fiction death) and the Judge, "newcomer to The Executive's Club", takes his place (wwa-1998-01-02), the night Mr. Business is first seen with the club. From then the Outlaw, the Executive, Mr. Business and the Judge are seated together at the Saloon table (wwa-1997-01-09), and the cards speak of "the rest of the Executive's Club" and, on 23 January 1998, "all four members of the Executive's Club" (wwa-1998-01-23). The record first held only the two men who wrestled as a tag team; that pair is now its own record, the-executive-and-mr-business-wwa, and holds the CWC Northeast Tag Team Championship reign. units.name: The Fallen

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the team from /promotions/maw-10-simple-rules/archive/show-beach-blast-2010-07-p209-211.html.

units.caption: The group of Firebird, the former Ultimate Phoenix, who preaches that a man must fall to the bottom of his soul before he can understand goodness. Its three masked newcomers, Ricochet, Sharp and Toxin, ambush Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Mother, May I? in May 2010; Firebird himself breaks with The Watch at Summer Showdown that June, offers The Firm a truce at Beach Blast, and at Eleventh Hour in November has the three unmask as Marc Speed, Greg Ford and Joey Poison, while the newcomer Evil Spirit stands at his side. By April 2011 Firebird lists his followers as Thrash, Greg Ford, Marc Speed, Evil Spirit and JD Morgan, and says that another is to come: Thrash arrives at All Or Nothing in February, JD Morgan is signed to join them, Evil Spirit takes Firebird's side against his former master Fumihiro Ota, and Black Eagle is welcomed back at April Showers. At Mother, May I? on 26th May 2011 Firebird presents the converted Masked Patriot as Providence, the fourth of the four men, with Black Eagle and JD Morgan, who have "something greater"; Greg Ford and Marc Speed still work for the light in their own way. Firebird and Providence beat Aaron Andrews and Kirk Jameson at Summer Showdown, and a Fallen trio led by Morgan loses the Trios titles match against The Firm at Back To School. At Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 Firebird announces, after Kirk Jameson has turned his back on the Fall, that The Fallen will no longer pursue one man and will be everywhere; JD Morgan breaks away to win the All Action title as his own man. With Black Eagle in hospital, Firebird calls in Father Johan at Spring Fever on 12th April 2012 as an ally to strengthen the ranks, and from May The Force Be With You on 5th May the two fight side by side. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 the name is Firebird's again, with Father Johan, Black Eagle and Providence; at Summer Showdown on 12th June Fumihiro Ota, who from Hotter Than Hot wishes to be called The Great Ota, attacks Donnie J and joins them, and Aaron Andrews shakes Father Johan's hand after swinging the Heavyweight belt into Kirk Jameson's head. The six men come to the ring together at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, Andrews saying that they will ensure he remains the Heavyweight champion; they fight Kirk Jameson's Knights Templar, Firebird and Ota blindsiding Jameson and Bradford Peverell at South East Grand Parade on 9th August, they lose Father Johan on 12th July, when he and KC Glenn fall from the turnbuckle, and they lose Black Eagle, with Sienna LeNoir, when their contracts expire in September; at Back To School on 5th September Andrews tells them that the group does not work without him as champion.

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the team from /promotions/maw-10-simple-rules/archive/show-all-or-nothing-2008-02-p16-19.html.

units.caption: Jean Cattley's faction, which grows to take in Casey Valentine, Cameron Vessey, Ricky Douglas and Davis Wayne Newton, beats down anyone who resists it, and drops Newton after Iron. Ricky Douglas is thrown out at End Of Days in December 2008 and Primus Allen takes his place. Darryl Devine and Ryan Powell join in March 2010; Jean Cattley, Devine and Powell become the first MAW Trios champions that month, and by April the faction carries the Tag Team titles (through Casey Valentine), the Trios titles and Primus Allen's Invitational trophy. Darryl Devine is gone out west by Summer Showdown in June 2010 and Primus Allen takes his place in the Trios team; Ryan Powell leaves for SWF in July and the Trios titles go at Hotter Than Hot. In August Jean Cattley warns Casey Valentine not to usurp him, and at Where It All Begins Again in October 2010 Cattley beats Valentine for control of the group: Primus Allen powerbombs Valentine and leaves, Jared Johnson leaves as well, and Cattley expels Valentine. The stable is reborn after Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011: Jean Cattley asks Steve Flash to keep his legacy going, and Flash gathers Chance Fortune, Randy Bumfhole and, as its fourth man, Kid Arachnid in the old Firm's dressing room, with a plan to confront the Second Sons and The Fallen. Arachnid, Fortune and Bumfhole win the Trios titles from The Triple Threat at Summernova on 12th August and keep them against The Fallen at Back To School. At All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011 Chance Fortune brings in Zimmy Bumfhole against the Second Sons, and at Where It All Begins Again the Trios titles go to the Second Sons. After Chance Fortune and Steve Flash leave for the SWF in November, Randy Bumfhole and Kid Arachnid, whom the narrator calls the remnants of The Firm, are left; Kirk Jameson tells Arachnid to strike out on his own.

tenures.note: First teamed on 21 March 2004, beating Fury (Rage and Spice). Billed together under this name on a 29 May 2004 card banner, beating the Fraternity Boys in a tag confrontation, then fighting the Ghost Dancers to a double countout in a formal tag match later the same card. Challenged for the UWF World Tag Team Championship in a Gold Rush triple threat on 5 June 2004 against champions the Privateers and the Ghost Dancers, taken out of the match by a triple Conchairto from the Fraternity Boys (Chris O'Brien and Brian McKenzie) before the Privateers stole the pinfall. Beat Kyle Lee and Alex Kidd in a steel cage main event on 28 August 2004, Caliban pinning Kidd with a Near Death Experience superplex-and-slam combination after Lee escaped the cage but could not return in time to help. Lost to Strictly Business (Andrew Tucker, Mike Sebastian) by pinfall on 2 October 2004 after Tucker's frozen-fish distraction; beaten down afterward by the returning Prophets of Rage with their own tag title belts. Billed as the new World Tag Team Champions as of 20 July 2005, having taken the titles from the Sons of Cacophony on the previous week's own unread Rampage (9 July 2005); no surviving document in the held record states the match itself. Caliban was kidnapped and chained up inside the Descent Into Hell structure by Erik Grimsson on 23 July 2005, who challenged the team to defend the titles there at Gold Rush. Lost with Trey DaMann to the Sons of Cacaphony and Corey Irons by pinfall on 3 August 2005, Irons pinning Caliban; recorded a Descent Into Hell promo, assaulted Nina Grimsson, and brutalized a non-competing Alex Extreme on 6 August 2005, then answered the Sons of Cacaphony's own ringside challenge with a taunting Unitron segment rather than a confrontation, singeing Erik Grimsson with pyrotechnics.

units.name: The Hardcore Innovators

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p967-1005.html.

units.caption: Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer, who team in April 2007 after Cactus, weeping backstage, saves Dreamer from Chris Benoit with a barbed-wire 2x4, and in May win the Hardcore Heaven match against Chris Benoit and The Sandman for the number one contendership to the World Tag Team Championship, when Cactus's Double Arm DDT pins Benoit as Dreamer drives The Sandman through a DDT on the concrete. Billed as 'The Hardcore Innovators' on Revolution in June 2007, they bring Singapore canes to the ring and win in turn over the Full Blooded Italians, over a second team on Blood, Sweat and Beers and on the next Revolution, and over Mark Briscoe, each time with a Double DDT. In June 2007 the Innovators beat Balls & Axl (Dreamer's Double DDT on Axl), the bWo (Cactus's Double Arm DDT on Stevie) and Paul London and Brian Kendrick, Cactus having been Super Kicked by Stevie in the car park; at Wrestlepalooza they lose the World Tag Team Championship Match to the Whole F**kin' Show and afterwards ask Heyman for the Dudleys. In July the Dudleys beat them for the number one contendership with Big Dick Dudley Jr.'s and Daizy's help, after attacking them with chairs and a 3D through a table; at Summer Assylum the Innovators DDT the champions after the Tables Match and are floored by Ultimo Dudley II, they lose to the champions in a non-title match on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and in August they DDT the whole second generation and challenge the Dudleys for the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles at Heatwave. In August 2007 they beat the bWo (a Double DDT on Hollywood Nova) on Revolution and Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II (a Double DDT on Ultimo Dudley II) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and after the Dudley Boyz beat the Briscoe Boys they cane the second generation of Dudleyz, DDT Bubba Ray and D-Von and take the Dudleyville Hardcore Title belts with them. At Heatwave they win the titles from the Dudley Boyz, whom they put through a table with a Double DDT, and the Whole F**kin' Show attack them afterwards; the diary then calls the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, 'newly rechristened'. In September, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, the Innovators ask the World Tag Team Champions for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz to crown the Undisputed Tag Team Champions, and Tommy Dreamer pins Rob Van Dam on Revolution when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick misses Dreamer and hits Van Dam. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest when the Dudley Family run in; Tommy Dreamer is pinned by D-Von on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In October, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, they ask Paul Heyman for a Singapore Cane Match, Dreamer's DDT beats Ultimo Dudley II, and at Guilty As Charged Cactus Jack and Dreamer are eliminated in the Three Way Dance (Bubba Ray pins Dreamer after Michaels's Sweet Chin Music and Cactus Jack after the Whole F**kin' Show's 420 Splash through a table), losing the Dudleyville belts, but they leave with all four tag belts and beat the second generation of Dudleyz with a Double DDT the next night before taking the belts from ringside again. In November 2007 the Innovators carry all four tag belts to the ring and beat Brandon Thomaselli with a Double DDT on Blood, Sweat and Beers; Tommy Dreamer and Cactus Jack say that at November To Remember XV they will win both tag titles and leave as the first Undisputed ECW Tag Team Champions, and Paul Heyman books the match against the Dudley Boyz to unify the titles. They beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz with a Double DDT on the last Revolution before the pay-per-view, and join the eight-man brawl that ends that show with Singapore canes. At November To Remember XV the Innovators come to the ring with Singapore canes and lose to the Dudley Boyz, Tommy Dreamer taking a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table while Cactus Jack and Beulah McGillicutty lie beaten; the Dudley Boyz raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles. Cactus Jack's promo that night accuses Nate Hatred of maiming the men who paved the way for him and warns that 'when you insult one Hardcore Innovator, you insult them both'. Dreamer loses his Masters of Pain qualifying match to Chris Hero on the Saturday show when Hatred knocks him out with a Decapitator Lariat; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Cactus Jack is ruled knocked out in his qualifier with Mark Calaway after Hatred hits both men with Decapitator Lariats, and Hatred floors both Innovators with a Double Decapitator. On the Saturday show Hatred beats Dreamer, and James Mitchell books a handicap match against both at Got Blood?; Cactus's promo calls himself 'the cripple' who 'actually enjoys that pain'.

In April 2007 Raven fires Owen Hart as commissioner; Owen beats Kensuke Sasaki with a Sharpshooter in the semi-final of the Number One Contendership Tournament and loses the final to Rhino when the masked man's chair misses Raven and hits him, while Bret beats Goliath at Cyberslam for a title shot. In May the brothers fall out: after beating Paul London and Brian Kendrick with matching Sharpshooters Bret pulls Owen off a cover, and Paul Heyman makes their Hardcore Heaven match the number one contendership, which Owen wins with a Diving Headbutt; in June Heyman books Owen against Raven at Wrestlepalooza and Bret in a Triangle Match for the title. In June 2007 the brothers argue on Revolution over who will take the World Heavyweight Championship, Bret calling Owen's Hardcore Heaven win a fluke, and Bret beats Doug Williams with the Sharpshooter; at Wrestlepalooza they take turns with the Sharpshooter and the Ankle Lock in the Triangle Match with Raven, Owen makes Bret tap, and Raven then pins Owen with a Raven Effect onto a chair and keeps the belt. Bret does not appear again in this run; Owen beats Lance Storm with the Sharpshooter on Blood, Sweat and Beers after Summer Assylum, is mocked there by Chris Jericho, challenges Jericho for Heatwave, and in August beats Chris Hero with a Sharpshooter in the tag match with Jerry Lynn.

units.notes: THE LINE: a uewf tenure is warranted where a held document BILLS THE ENTITY AS THAT FEDERATION'S OWN, or STAGES IT FOR ONE OF THAT FEDERATION'S OWN CHAMPIONSHIPS. Entry to a tournament held at an interfederation event is not by itself enough — the Summit's tournaments were open to all comers and a bracket slot says only that somebody entered. WHAT SETTLES THIS ROW: NO uewf TENURE FOR THE TEAM, deliberately, though both the wrestler and the manager attached to it have one. The rule turns on what a document bills, and what the UeWF's own record bills is Mosh the singles competitor: it ranked him, and it staged him against Biff Jones for its Atlantic Heavyweight Championship on 19 February 1992. The team name appears in one UeWF sentence and it is an opponent's taunt — "your FOOLs Meatball and Flintstone got run out of the UeWF because they're afraid of the Headbangers" (13 April 1992) — which implies the team was around without the federation ever billing it. The Headbangers do not stand in the UeWF's own tag rankings. Recorded here so the asymmetry reads as a decision, not an oversight.

units.name: The Iron Saints

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-08-p111-166.html.

units.caption: A stable of preaching youngsters who arrive on F' The Mainstream in August 2006 vowing to rid ECW of sinners, call out one wrestler a week for punishment, and win the First Blood Match against The Acolytes at Heatwave. In February 2007 the Iron Saints, Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli, beat the Dudley Boys, the Blue World Order and the FBI in a row, jump the Whole F**kin' Show on Blood, Sweat and Beers and throw Traci through a table, and take the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships at Living Dangerously with a Spike Powerbomb on Shawn Michaels after Rob Van Dam steps off the apron; they lose the belts at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match and in April beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick. In April 2007 the Iron Saints beat the Full Blooded Italians, lose to the Canadian Connection and then to Monsters Inc with the Nest's interference, after which Raven orders Vito to hit one of his own brothers with a Vito Driver. In May they object to Vito bringing their sister Kelly into ECW, side with Paul Burchill against the Nest (Salvatore is the masked man on Blood, Sweat and Beers), beat Vito and CM Punk, beat the Nest in a six-man tag with Burchill and lose to Vito and Punk on Revolution; at Hardcore Heaven they beat Monsters Inc with steel chairs, then are chokeslammed and taken away on gurneys after Vito turns on them. On Revolution in June 2007 Brandon and Salvatore return from hospital with chairs and wreck the Nest as Paul Burchill is about to be powerbombed through tables; at Wrestlepalooza Vito turns on CM Punk and, with his brothers, beats him in the tag match Heyman gave them. In July Raven makes them wrestle each other (Brandon wins with a T-Bone Suplex and Salvatore hugs him), Mark Calaway beats Brandon with a Chokeslam in the tag match against Vito and Calaway, and at Summer Assylum the Saints beat CM Punk and Monsters Inc. In August Brandon beats Afa and Salvatore saves him from the Samoan Gangstas. In August 2007 Brandon is beaten by Nate Hatred when James Mitchell's cane intervenes, and both brothers are at ringside with Vito when Raven's Nest turn on him. In September Sal beats Chris Jericho with a Tiger Driver, Brandon is beaten by Rhino and by Paul Burchill, Sal is beaten by Burchill, and the brothers come to Burchill's aid with Vito and Kelly. In October 2007 Sal beats Jerry Lynn with a Senton Bomb, and the brothers announce 'Thomaselli Thomaselli '08', the Green Party's candidacy for president; Brandon wins the 'Presidential Primary' Match against Yoshihiro Tajiri with a T-Bone suplex, and Sal loses to Kurt Angle's Ankle Lock. In November 2007 Brandon beats Scorpio Sky with a Crossface Chickenwing and Sal beats Teddy Hart with a Senton Bomb on the first F' The Mainstream recap; the brothers lose to the Hardcore Innovators (a Double DDT on Brandon) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, Sal loses to Shawn Michaels's Sweet Chin Music, to Chris Hero, who then chokes him out, and to Andrew Martin in a parody gimmick, and Brandon loses to Nate Hatred's Decapitator Lariat and to Martin in a second parody. At November To Remember XV Vito beats CM Punk clean with a Vito Driver and walks to the ring in Paul Burchill's entourage with his sister Kelly, Steven Regal and Shane Douglas. Sal and Brandon wrestle as Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08: on Revolution on the first Monday of December they lose the Three Way Dance for the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; the F' The Mainstream recap has Jushin Lyger and Rey Mysterio Jr. beat them in 9:22, and on the Saturday show Slyk and Dick Dudley beat them with a Boston Crabs on Brandon before the Original Dudleyz chair Brandon and powerbomb Sal through a table. Vito and Burchill beat CM Punk and Goliath by disqualification on Revolution, and on the Saturday show Rhino beats Vito in a number one contendership match.

units.name: The Masked Patriot and Kashmir Singh

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the team from /promotions/maw-10-simple-rules/archive/month-2008-04-p25-25.html.

units.caption: A babyface tag team the narrator finds excellent, introduced at Spring Fever against Citizen X and Findlay O'Farraday. With the Masked Patriot now wrestling as "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith, the pair beat Ricochet & Sharp at Summer Showdown in June 2010, and with Fumihiro Ota they are the Trios champions; the diary's own title records call them "Smith & Singh", and the narrator's roster overview says he has "formed a great tag team" for the coming months. As Smith & Singh they lose to the Canadian Blondes at Remember November in November 2010 and at the Invitational, lose to Ford & Speed at All Or Nothing in February 2011, beat Casey Valentine and Antonio on the 25th March tour show and fall to The Triple Threat with Amazing Fire Fly on 4th April. They lose the Tag Team title three-ways of 26th May and 12th July 2011, lose to Ford & Speed at Summernova, squash Team XDW at Iron and, with Fumihiro Ota, beat the Canadian Blondes and Raphael at Back To School; Singh's Broadway enthusiasm and Smith's dyed hair run through July and August. Billed by the diary as Smith & Singh, they lose a three-way at Fall Of The King on 26th September 2011, win the Tag Team titles from the Canadian Blondes at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October, and keep them against the Second Sons, the Dark Raptors and Ford & Speed, Ford & Speed, Firebird and Citizen X and, at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012, Ford & Speed and Lockdown; Singh and Smith talk Broadway musicals through the winter. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 they keep the Tag Team titles against the Canadian Blondes at Great Lakes Crisis, the Second Sons at March Madness and the Second Sons again at May The Force Be With You, and before the Gold Rush match at April Showers agree to be friends and partners entering it but rivals bell to bell. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 they keep the Tag Team titles in the three-way at High Noon on 5th June, lose them to the Dark Raptors at Summer Showdown on 12th June, and then lose to Always Breakin' Hollywood, the Second Sons, the Canadian Blondes and Ford & Speed, the narrator saying they are doing the job to any heel team that needs a little love; at Back To School on 5th September they stand with Donnie J to protect Sienna LeNoir.

tenures.note: Wins the Dog Day Two tag team tournament, beating the Unholy Alliance and CAPSMEN! in the first round and Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone in the final, then competes in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Part of a six-man brawl with Capsmen, Iyasu Saku and Sonicman ruled a no contest on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004). Loses to Alcoholics Anonymous (Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen) by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after isolating an injured McQueen, then runs in to break up a Capsman near-fall on Real Deal during the VWF Tag Team Championship match, handing Blaze and Real Deal the disqualification win. The Salvation publicly refuses Kingston Cash's own proposed tag-title handicap-match stipulation on the team's behalf on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), then helps clear the ring after Adam Jennings retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship; The Reckoning loses a straight singles match to Mark McQueen the same night. Both men enter the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), The Salvation triple-teamed out by the Riders of the Apocalypse after The Reckoning leaves him to challenge mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov, who eliminates The Reckoning moments later. The Reckoning taps out to Kenny Kidd's own Ankle Lock on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), suffering ligament damage.

units.name: The New Extreme Order

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-10-p1441-1534.html.

units.caption: Nate Hatred, Chris Hero and James Mitchell, whom the diary bills as 'The New Extreme Order' when they walk to the ring on Blood, Sweat and Beers in October 2007 (and calls 'The New Blood' in the match before). Hero helps Hatred beat Paul Burchill at Anarchy Rulz, with the Decapitator Lariat, and the Sinister Minister, Hero and Hatred celebrate with a hug; Hero costs Bret Hart his match with Hatred and, in a handicap match with Hatred, rolls Bret up with his feet on the ropes; Hatred beats Sabu on Blood, Sweat and Beers and on Revolution with Hero's help, and Mitchell challenges Sabu to a Streak versus Career Match at November To Remember XV. In November 2007 Nate Hatred, with James Mitchell, interferes in the Mark Calaway and Sabu match on Revolution, beats Calaway and Sabu with Rhino on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and has Mitchell promise Sabu his 'day of judgement' in the Streak versus Career Match at November To Remember XV; Hatred beats Brandon Thomaselli with the Decapitator Lariat, and after Sabu beats Masato Tanaka he wraps barbed wire round Sabu's neck and hangs him over the ropes, the broadcast cutting away, and on the last Revolution a mannequin of Hatred hangs from barbed wire and burns in a corridor. Chris Hero, who calls himself 'The Saviour of ECW', beats Chris Jericho twice in three nights, Jerry Lynn and Sal Thomaselli, and with Punk beats Jericho and Vito on Blood, Sweat and Beers. At November To Remember XV Nate Hatred, with James Mitchell, beats Sabu in the Streak versus Career Match with a Big Splash onto barbed wire and a Decapitator Lariat and spits at Sabu's offered hand, and Chris Hero beats Chris Jericho with Hero's Welcome after a Liontamer. On the Saturday show Hero beats Tommy Dreamer in a Masters of Pain qualifier when Hatred knocks Dreamer out; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Hatred and Mitchell break up Cactus Jack's qualifier with Mark Calaway, Hatred hitting both men with Decapitator Lariats so that Cactus is ruled knocked out, and he floors both Innovators with a Double Decapitator. On the Saturday show Hero beats Eddie Guerrero with Hero's Sidekick, and Hatred beats Dreamer; Mitchell announces a handicap match against both Innovators at Got Blood?, and Hatred smashes a microphone handle into his own forehead until he bleeds.

The team's own claim to being "7-time GIWF tag team champions" doesn't reconcile with the registry's own count of 6 real reigns (3x World Tag Team + 3x North American Tag Team, all in data/reigns.json) — the seventh is the foam "Universal Tag Team" belt they gave themselves and, per the user's own account, glorified above all 6 of their actual title wins. Receipted: their own GIWF bio page describes each man as "always" wearing his "Universal Tag Team Title belt" in the physical-appearance prose — conspicuously absent from the SAME bio's own Accomplishments list a few paragraphs later, which sticks to the 6 real reigns. units.name: The Second Sons

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the team from /promotions/maw-10-simple-rules/archive/show-spring-fever-2011-04-p333-337.html.

units.caption: Erik Strong, Antonio and Casey Valentine, who name themselves at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 after Casey Valentine's Loser Leaves Town win over Jean Cattley, telling Cattley that they are the men who should be in charge of the company now. Jay Chord refuses to join them and warns them to change the name, and the narrator's e-mails tell Jay to think about what "Second Sons" could mean in the company. They feud with Steve Flash's new Firm through the summer: Strong and Chord beat Flash and Kid Arachnid on 12th May, Valentine and Antonio beat Randy Bumfhole and Arachnid on 26th May, the three-match series at High Noon on 12th June ends one win each and a time-limit draw, Flash beats Valentine again at Summer Showdown and Antonio at Hotter Than Hot, where the Sons ambush Flash and Bumfhole after the bell, and Antonio and Strong lose to Flash and Bumfhole at Beach Blast. Jay Chord, Valentine and Antonio, billed as the Second Sons, beat Fumihiro Ota and the Young Americans at Summernova on 12th August, and Valentine and Antonio beat the Young Americans at Back To School; in September Strong tells the narrator that he has an offer to go back up north. With Jay Chord and Erik Strong gone, Antonio and Casey Valentine are joined by Cameron Vessey, on loan from USPW, at All The Leaves Are Brown on 12th October 2011, where the three jump Chance Fortune and Zimmy Bumfhole; they win the Trios titles from The Firm at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October, Valentine pinning Kid Arachnid, and lose them when Rip Chord retires the belts at Eleventh Hour on 12th November, JD Morgan throwing out all three in the battle royal for the All Action title. Antonio and Valentine lose to Smith & Singh for the Tag Team titles at Remember November, beat the West Texas Peacekeepers at End Of Days, and lose to Wanda Fish and Jared Johnson on 5th January 2012; Valentine says that the pair will rely on themselves. In the diary's pages from March to May 2012 they beat the Internet Favourites at Third Time's The Charm, lose a Tag Team title match to Smith & Singh at March Madness, win a four-team match at April Showers on 5th April to earn a title shot, win the Spring Fever three-way and lose the title match to Smith & Singh at May The Force Be With You on 5th May. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 they lose the High Noon three-way on 5th June, beat Team Honor at Summer Showdown and Smith & Singh at Beach Blast, and lose at South East Grand Parade with Black Eagle and in the three-way at Iron on 12th August.

units.caption: Jake and Ric Shield of Russell, Ontario, who teamed with Johann Svenson at the second Summit against the men who had jumped two of their friends, and spent the following summer as the PWA’s top-ranked tag team without ever taking its belts — beaten twice by Da Boyz and once by the Dogs of War.

identity.note: Shares a team name with other registry "Shield"-named entities and the real-world WWE stable The Shield; nothing beyond the bare label is shared with either — filed distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

units.notes: Receipt: the Summit of E-Wrestling’s own third night of 29 December 1991 announces the pair together — “hailing from Russell, Ontario, Canada, weighing in at 244 pounds, Jake “Canadian” Shield! And also from Russell, weighing in at 278 pounds, Ric “Tower” Shield!” — and the PWA’s own 1992 record announces the Shield Brothers “hailing from Russell, Ontario, Canada” and puts them in the ring against Da Boyz and their manager Da Boss, the same team under the same manager the Summit’s own card had staged eleven months earlier. Same hometown, same brother pair, same team name, same opponents. The PWA tenure above is folded in from that row; data/aliases.json redirects the retired id to this one. The retired row’s own with-less “distinct” guard against the real-world WWE stable The Shield is carried over unchanged. A third receipt, carried back from the pwa-1992 reciprocal guard main filed the same day and now superseded by this merge: the UFWS’s own Report #13 of 6 August 1991 has Jake Shield say “I will be leaving the UFWS soon, to start training my younger brother for the ring.” Five months later the Summit of E-Wrestling’s own third night announces the two of them together out of Russell, Ontario; eleven months after that the PWA announces the same team out of the same town. The 1991 guard called the younger brother an inference; the hometown the two feds announce is not one.

units.caption: Big Stevie Cool and The Great Sasuke, who turn on their own groups at Guilty As Charged in October 2007: when the bWo and the sWo meet in an eight-man tag with the loser to disband, Big Stevie Cool Stevie Kicks Hollywood Nova, BW Snow and Ozz after Sasuke has pinned Nova, Sasuke Superkicks Chessman, and Stevie says that he was the masked 'mole' who had been attacking the bWo, that the two of them are 'the only respectable wrestlers in this whole bunch', that the angle is 'a parody of a parody' and that they are 'the TRUE World Order'. The diary's previews bill them as Stevie Richards and The Great Sasuke; they make their debut as a team on Blood, Sweat and Beers against London and Kendrick and win when Sasuke hits a Michinoku Driver on Kendrick. In November 2007 Sasuke and Stevie Richards beat Mark Briscoe with a Michinoku Driver on Revolution; Stevie interferes against Rob Van Dam and Sasuke is pinned by Van Dam's 420 Splash, the two attack Shawn Michaels after he beats Sal Thomaselli until Van Dam saves him with a chair and the Van Daminator, and they lose to the Whole F**kin' Show on Revolution. On the Saturday show after November To Remember XV The Great Sasuke says that he was 'given f**king sWo angle' and 'stranded with face-paint Mexican freaks for a year', and loses to Juventud Guerrera's Juvi Driver; the F' The Mainstream recap has the True World Order beat 'Masked & Magnificent' in 8:43 after a Stevie Kick. On the Saturday show of the first week of December Sasuke loses to Rob Van Dam's Van Daminator in a Masters of Pain qualifier, and Stevie Richards, who calls Sasuke his new partner, is stopped by Shawn Michaels's Sweet Chin Music.

units.name: The Whole F**kin' Show

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-11-p386-412.html.

units.caption: Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels, the Show Stealer and the Showstopper, who team on Revolution in November 2006, beat the Acolytes, take the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships from Monsters Inc. at November To Remember with the 420 Splash, make Traci their manager and keep the belts through January and February 2007 while the two partners fall out over her. The partners fall out at Living Dangerously when Rob Van Dam steps off the apron and lets the Iron Saints pin Shawn Michaels for the belts, make up the next night on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Michaels explains himself, trap the Iron Saints with Traci's help, and win the belts back at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match with a Five Star Frog Splash on Salvatore; in April Rob Van Dam and Traci kiss, and Rob Van Dam is booked against Chris Jericho for the Television Championship at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam in April 2007 Rob Van Dam beats Chris Jericho for the Television Championship in the Lumberjack Match and the team keep the tag belts in the Ladder Match against Los Increibles. In May AJ Styles's debut and Rob Van Dam's jealousy over Traci split the partners, and at Hardcore Heaven Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone, keeps the tag belts over the Canadian Connection with a third Sweet Chin Music on Christian while Van Dam is away helping Traci; Van Dam then loses the Television Championship to AJ Styles, helped by the Canadian Connection's hockey sticks. In June Van Dam and Michaels refuse to tag each other and Michaels slaps Van Dam, then Traci locks them in a locker room and they make up. In June 2007 Van Dam and Michaels make peace with the Hardcore Innovators, trading hugs and signs on each other's backs, and at Wrestlepalooza keep the World Tag Team Championship over them when Michaels's Diving Elbow and Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash win simultaneous covers, before the Dudley Boys, back in ECW, attack them. At Summer Assylum they win the Tables Match against the Dudleys with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table on D-Von, are DDT'd by the Innovators afterwards, beat the Innovators on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Ultimo Dudley II hits Cactus Jack with a lid, and in August Traci is pranked by the bWo. At Heatwave in August 2007 they run out after the Innovators win the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles and attack Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer with a Superkick, an Enziguiri, a Flying Elbow Drop and a Five Star Frog Splash, telling them there is room for only one World Tag Team Champions; the Dudley Family and the Innovators then brawl with them in a no contest on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In September they keep the belts over the Dudley Boyz on Revolution with simultaneous finishers, Shawn Michaels pins D-Von with a Super Kick the week after, and they accept the Innovators' challenge for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz. When Michaels walks in on Traci changing and covers her as footsteps approach, Rob Van Dam takes the wrong meaning and the partners fall out for two weeks, Van Dam leaving Michaels alone against the Dudleyz in a non-title match, until they hug it out backstage on the last Monday before the pay-per-view. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest after the Dudley Family run in. In October Traci is carried out on a stretcher after the Dudleyz drop her onto the guard rail while Michaels and Van Dam are distracted, and the partners quarrel over which stipulation to ask for until Paul Heyman books a match with ladders, chairs, canes and flaming tables; at Guilty As Charged Michaels shoves D-Von through a burning table, then his Super Kick catches Van Dam in mid-air and Bubba Ray pins Van Dam, ending the reign. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Van Dam punches Michaels and later calls for a reunion, and Michaels hugs him and Super Kicks him again ('that Super Kick last night was no accident and nor was this'). In November 2007 Shawn Michaels apologises on Revolution for the Super Kick at Guilty As Charged and calls Rob Van Dam his brother; Van Dam asks for a one-on-one match and, when Michaels says that he cannot fight his brother, hits him with the Van Daminator and a chair, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers he appears at the entrance to distract Michaels in his match with CM Punk. Michaels refuses the match again, but the two save each other from the True World Order and beat it together on Revolution, and Paul Heyman, 'sorry to go over your head', books Rob Van Dam against Shawn Michaels at November To Remember XV; on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers before it they are on opposite sides of a tag match and still join to beat down Kurt Angle, and on the last Revolution they jump off opposite corners together onto the brawl that wrecks the ring. At November To Remember XV Shawn Michaels and Rob Van Dam walk to the ring together to Pantera and trade a contest of alphabet moves (RVD: 'It's November 2007, bro... they're on strike') before the match the diary rates A: Michaels beats Van Dam with a Sweet Chin Music that drives into his face the chair Van Dam is carrying, and both bow to the crowd. On Revolution on the first Monday of December Van Dam hugs Michaels backstage and says he wants a rematch, 'since we're both in Masters of Pain Qualifiers'; on the Saturday show Van Dam beats The Great Sasuke by knockout after the Van Daminator, Stevie Richards runs in and Michaels clears him with Sweet Chin Music.

Supported by primary sources: the IWF 1998 roster/Stable-of-the-Year record, and the GIWF's own Stable Wars honor-roll listing (2 Jun 1999) on the GIWF North American Tag Team title page.

VERDICT, THE IDENTITY WAVE (2026-08-22), verbatim: "merge the New Youngbloods." new-youngbloods-giwf (Lew Spectre & Lyle Wile, GIWF, 1999-2001, a 24-day World Tag Team Championship reign) folded into the-youngbloods — Lew Spectre already an IWF-era Youngblood, the GIWF billing scare-quoting itself "'New'" as a deliberate in-fiction continuity marker rather than an unrelated coincidence. Lyle Wile added to the roster as the GIWF-era member; the existing GIWF tenure entry (already on file, same 1999-2001 window) enriched with the reign detail rather than duplicated.

tenures.note: Named on commentary through Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), closing that broadcast standing together over a bloodied Lark Fenriz, Jason Storm and Classy Joey Boy after The Equalizer's own VWF Heavyweight Championship win. Wins a six-man tag over Jason Storm, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Flash on March To Hell (21 October 2004), the group's own Pagan unmasked on air for the first time. Briefly inducts Flash as a fourth member on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) before turning on him mid-promo and beating him unconscious; the same night Gods Tears wins a non-title count-out over The Maquilladora, boasting on air about the group's own formation, and Pagan is revealed as Melanie Kilpatrick's own kidnapper during the post-show chaos that follows Jason Storm's ambush of The Equalizer. Gods Tears wins the VWF Submission Championship and The Equalizer retains the VWF Heavyweight Championship in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Pagan interfering in the final fall after separately crippling Jason Storm in an unsanctioned cage trap.

tenures.role: tag team — PTC Tag Team Champions, won on the judges' scores for the three-way "Purgatory with a Pinata" match of April 2005 that no federation hosted and nobody ever wrote; the belts went to the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean the following month when the pair no-showed the defence
tenures.source: PTC's own forum (accession 0160), the alliance's own boards: "Tag Team Division Sign ups: March" (post 139843, topic 12956), 14 Mar 2005 — the team's own sign-up; "Tag Team Title Match" (post 142892, topic 13360), 1 Apr 2005 — the match's own announcement; "PTC Tag Team Titles Match Roleplaying" (posts 144529 and 144903, topic 13478), 11-12 Apr 2005 — the card and the pair's own roleplay "Nightlife"; "PTC Tag Title Match" (post 147097, topic 13686), 26 Apr 2005 — the judges' scores and the title ruling; "PTC Tag Title Match" (posts 148625 and 149811, topic 13774) and "Tag Open Challenge?" (post 150691, topic 13767), 6-22 May 2005 — the defence against the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean; "PTC Title Histories (Back to PIT)" (post 170694, topic 15747), 27 Oct 2005 — the alliance's own title lineage; and "Top Ten Matches Your Character Was In" (post 199384, topic 17963), 30 May 2006 — the Killer Pirates' own account of how the reign ended. Corroborated outside the board by PTC's own encyclopedia (promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-seymour-almasy.html and -2008.html) and by PRIME's own roleplay "The Nobody Puts Up His Dukes, Part III" of 11 May 2005 (promotions/prime-2003/rp/the-nobody-puts-up-his-dukes-part-iii-et-match-overkill-2005-05-11.html).
tenures.note: The team's whole life, from the board's own posts. They signed up for the alliance's March 2005 tag division as "Unholy Matrimony", billed from the UWF, the sign-up naming them "The Final Fantasy" Seymour Almasy and "The One Winged Angel" Aerith Almasy, and were put straight into a three-way for the PTC Tag Team Championship: "Six Kendo Sticks. Three tag teams. Two gold belts. One pinata. Zaro chance of anyone leaving with their dignity intact. This is... Purgatory with a Pinata~!", against the champions, billed Los Muchos Macho Mascadas (White Tiger and Pajaro de Presa, also of the UWF), and Soul Purpose (Noah Hanson and Fury, of WMW). One roleplay each was the limit. NO MATCH WAS EVER WRITTEN: no federation offered to host it after weeks of asking, and the championship changed hands on the judges' scores alone — two of the three judges placed Unholy Matrimony first and the third named only a second and a third place, and the ruling, posted 26 April 2005, reads "Sean is the new Tag Team Champion defeating the others." THE REIGN ENDED WITHOUT A MATCH OF ITS OWN EITHER: the Killer Pirates from the Outer Caribbean were booked against them through May 2005, and the Pirates' own side wrote a year later, listing his best matches, "PTC Tag Team Championship - Killer Pirates vs. Unholy Matrimony. Despite the no show by my opponents, I won the PTC Tag Team Championship belts". The alliance's own title history, posted 27 October 2005, places them sixth in the PTC Tag Team Championship's order, between the Masked Monkeys (Pajaro de Presa and White Tiger) and the Killer Pirates, and records the championship itself as discontinued and retired. THE REIGN IS RECORDED with the championship's other reigns, from 26 April 2005, the day of the ruling, to 28 May 2005, when the Killer Pirates took the belts uncontested: the history post gives an order and no dates — "I don't have dates. I just have orders of champions" — and both dates are PTC's own title log's, the first also the ruling post's. FOUR MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT THIS TEAM, checked and carrying no edge: Global Championship Wrestling's own roleplay "The Wheels Go 'Round 'n 'Round" of 1 October 2008 uses "that unholy matrimony" as the ordinary English phrase, for a wished-for combination of one wrestler's old ring skills with his current blood lust, and names neither member; so do FAW's "The Best Ideas are Often the Simplest" (16 October 2002, a stench), NAPW's "Phenoms Return" (April 2014, a suburban marriage) and a PTC roleplay of 9 January 2007 ("Lets make unholy matrimony with the belt on the line").

The decorated-aka guard reads this name against the registry's bare "Unholy" entities. Recorded as a separate team from unholy-cswa (CSWA) and unholy-dwo (the DWO): unrelated promotions, no shared member, and nothing in any of the three records connecting them. The overlap is the ordinary English phrase this team's own roleplay plays on, and says out loud: "It...is sort of sacrilegious, isn't it."

units.caption: Seymour Almasy and Aerith Heartilly's divorced-couple tag team, a pairing that had held the UWF World Tag Team Championship for four weeks in 2003 before it took the name and, in April 2005, the PTC Tag Team Championship on the judges' scores for a three-way pinata match no federation ever hosted — champions no longer a month later, when they no-showed the Killer Pirates of the Outer Caribbean.
units.notes: The name is Seymour Almasy's own invention and the pair's own roleplay stages him coining it — "do you like the name I came up with for us?" — with Aerith reading it back: "It...is sort of sacrilegious, isn't it. We're divorced, and yet we can't keep our hands off of each other. We love each other, and yet we remain in lust. Our lives are lived in physicality, both carnal with one another, and violent in competition." That roleplay, "Nightlife" of 12 April 2005, is the team's only surviving text of its own, and it is written by the same hand as both characters: it was posted from the memorial subject's own account on the board, the account already on his memorial row. It dates their teaming earlier than the name — Almasy calls her "the best tag team partner I've ever had" and recalls her pinning to win them the UWF World Tag Team Championship, the reign both their own records already carry (16 November - 14 December 2003) — and it gives her a submission of her own, the Cactuar Crossface, and a spell in XUDF before she came back. The pairing is billed from the UWF throughout, but no held UWF document bills them under this team name.

A separate entity from vegas-connection-wwo (WWO), not a merge — reciprocal to that row's own guard, filed here 2026-09-02 after the PRODIGY diaspora's second wave flagged the pair as unguarded on this side. The identity-join test settles it from both feds' own text rather than from silence. MEMBERS: this team is Aaron Reno and Steven Gage — the AAWC's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) ring announcer, "along with their manager Lady Luck! They are making their return to the AAWC! Here are Aaron Reno and Steven Gage...THE VEGAS CONNECTION!" WWO's team is a different two men entirely: that fed's own tag-team roster page bills "Vegas Connection — 'Lounge Lizard' Lester Leary and Larry Lowbrow", a lounge-act pairing managed by Rimshot, and each man's own bio card names the other as his tag partner. ERA AND PLATFORM: this team runs 1995-96 on the PRODIGY boards; WWO's holds that fed's World Tag Team titles in 2001 on a web-hosted site. PRIOR FEDS: WWO's own bio card for Larry Lowbrow lists where that team had been — the ECCWF, the STWF, the MBC and the PMCW/RCCW/BDCW — and names neither the AAWC nor the CSWA. Four different men, two different managers, five years and two platforms apart, with the WWO team's own travelogue excluding this one's feds. DISTINCT on the documents, not merely unjoined.

units.name: Vegas Connection

identity.note: A separate entity from vegas-connection (AAWC), not a merge. Re-verified 2026-09-02 on the identity-join test and UPGRADED from presumed to primary-source: the earlier filing rested on "no corroborating link beyond the shared name", but both feds' own documents name their own team's members, and the two memberships do not overlap. This team is "Lounge Lizard" Lester Leary and Larry Lowbrow — WWO's own tag-team roster page bills them under this name, each man's own bio card gives "Tag Team Name: The Vegas Connection" and names the other as his partner, and both are led by the manager Rimshot. The AAWC's team is Aaron Reno and Steven Gage, walked out by the manager Lady Luck on that fed's own Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1) card of 25 October 1996. Different eras and platforms too — the AAWC pair runs 1995-96 on the PRODIGY boards, this one holds the WWO World Tag Team titles in 2001 — and this row's own bio-card travelogue of where the team had been (the ECCWF, the STWF, the MBC, the PMCW/RCCW/BDCW) names neither the AAWC nor the CSWA. tenures.source: "WAR!ZONE" (11 Feb 1997, served): Alan Brunswick pins Matt Powers (Kalifornia Heat) to win the International WAR! Tag Team Championship, w/Ms.America & JJM. "WAR!CORE" (20 Feb 1997, collected) names Brunswick's partner Jeff Borbone during a title defense against Phantasmagoria that ends by DQ after a claw-hold angle leaves Brunswick comatose ("the soul of the All-Americans"). "SKIRMISH REPORT!" (24 Feb 1997, collected) has Borbone, with Jumbo Jim Mongol at ringside, retain the titles in a steel cage defense against the Windy City Warriors while Brunswick remains hospitalized, and anticipates Mongol standing in for him in a rematch.
